author: lbirts
body:
# Description
This PR is a frontend interview task that introduces a dedicated Secrets Management page, extracting the functionality from the Pipeline Editor sidekick and promoting it to a top-level project resource. Previously, users were required to open a random pipeline to manage project-wide secrets; this change makes secrets easily discoverable and manageable from the main navigation bar.

Addresses github issue: https://github.com/mage-ai/mage-ai/issues/5180

**Key Changes:**
- Centralized Management: Added "Secrets" to the main left-hand navigation under the "Main" section.
- New Management UI: Created a standalone Secrets page and a side-panel "Creation Wizard" (using the before drawer pattern).
- Proactive Validation:
  - Implemented a Regex check (/^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$/) to ensure secret names are compatible with Python variable naming and YAML keys.
  - Added immediate visual feedback for invalid names using the project's danger styling.
- Scalable Pagination: Implemented strict backend pagination (limit and offset) to handle potentially large datasets.
  - Design Decision: Client-side search was explicitly omitted. Since the backend does not support filtering by name, implementing client-side search on paginated data would result in a broken UX (searching only the current page).
- Security: Secret values are masked (********) by default in the UI.


# How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] Navigation: Verified that clicking "Secrets" in the main sidebar correctly routes to /secrets.
- [x] API Integration: Confirmed secrets are successfully read created and deleted via the backend, not updated.
- [x] Validation: Verified the "Create" button correctly disables for invalid patterns (spaces, starting with numbers).
- [x] Actions: Verified that clicking the copy and delete successfully completes respective actions.
- [x] Pagination: Confirmed that "Per page" limits and page navigation correctly update the URL and trigger SWR re-fetches.

# Checklist
- [x] The PR is tagged with proper labels (bug, enhancement, feature, documentation)
  - I do not have permissions to add labels
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [ ] I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
  - I originally added unit tests for the Secrets feature; however, I observed that this introduced a regression in the CI/CD pipeline performance (increasing build/test time by ~10 minutes). To maintain pipeline efficiency, I have omitted them from this PR, but I am happy to discuss strategies for optimizing the test infrastructure to support them in the future.
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a small Python utility that logs connectivity outages and performs periodic speed tests so users can document poor ISP performance.  
- Use a reputable public endpoint for measurements and make the tool configurable and scriptable for real-world monitoring and reporting.

### Description

- Add `internet_monitor/monitor.py` implementing `check_internet`, `_measure_transfer_speed`, `run_speed_test`, `monitor`, `setup_logger`, and a CLI via `build_parser`/`main`; it uses Cloudflare endpoints (`__down`/`__up`) and Google's generate_204 for connectivity checks.  
- Measure download/upload by streaming or POSTing a payload, compute Mbps, and log status changes and speed test results to a file via `setup_logger`.  
- Add package metadata file `internet_monitor/__init__.py` and `internet_monitor/README.md` with usage instructions and options such as `--check-interval`, `--speedtest-interval`, and `--once`.  
- Add unit tests in `tests/test_internet_monitor.py` that mock `requests` to cover connectivity checks, speed measurement logic, and logging of speed test failures.

### Testing

- Add two compact controls in the header: a theme toggle and a language toggle, and make language global/ persistent across the app. 
- Provide bilingual (ES/EN) copy so the UI updates immediately when the language is changed. 
- Keep accessibility and small visual footprint for header controls with proper `aria` labels.

- Introduces a `LanguageProvider` with localStorage persistence and `document.documentElement.lang` updates in `components/language-provider.tsx` and wraps the app in it via `app/layout.tsx`.

- Moves all home page copy into a new `content/home-copy.ts` object (English and Spanish) and refactors `app/page.tsx` to consume `useLanguage()` and `homeCopy` so copy changes immediately when toggling language. 
- Wires project and experience links to `href` values in the copy object and keeps existing styling and structure intact.

### Testing
- Ran the dev server with `npm run dev -- --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000` and the app compiled and served the home page successfully (`GET / 200`).

- `lib/bank/aiCategorisation.ts` - Core AI categorization service
- `lib/bank/aiLearning.ts` - Learning database management

### Motivation
- Simplificar a modelagem de presença removendo o estado "Não vou" e permitir que o usuário deixe um evento sem status ao clicar novamente na mesma opção. 
- Ter uma etapa leve para capturar *como* a pessoa vai (ex.: folião / vou tocar / apoio) sem ainda integrar usuário remoto; persistir essa escolha localmente. 
- Melhorar a usabilidade do drawer com informações de data/hora mais explícitas, ações ícone para copiar/abrir mapa e exibição dos gêneros como tags.

With `cmaize_find_or_build_dependency`, the `NAME` field is used to help match to the actual dependency name (like for casing/formatting quirks). body:
This pull request introduces several improvements to build tooling, dependency management, favicon and manifest support, and UI/UX enhancements for content reading components. The most significant changes include refactoring the `Makefile` to delegate commands to a Node script, updating dependencies and scripts in `package.json`, adding comprehensive favicon and manifest files, and improving the reading experience with better section tracking and smooth exit animations.

**Build tooling and dependency updates:**

* Refactored the `Makefile` to delegate all commands to `makefile.mjs`, simplifying command management and removing colorized help output. New targets for type checking and pre-commit hooks were added. (`[MakefileL1-R7](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52L1-R7)`)
* Updated `app/package.json` with new scripts for concurrent build and preview (`watch`), preview on port 3000, and added several dev dependencies such as `concurrently`, `nodemon`, `vite-plugin-checker`, and others. Also, moved `@tailwindcss/vite` to devDependencies, removed `react-icons`, and updated several package versions. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-012b982f97a0d326aeec58dd3b789484b05a944d609afe1b8ed5e299fc485f61R11-R13)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-012b982f97a0d326aeec58dd3b789484b05a944d609afe1b8ed5e299fc485f61L51)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-012b982f97a0d326aeec58dd3b789484b05a944d609afe1b8ed5e299fc485f61L67)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-012b982f97a0d326aeec58dd3b789484b05a944d609afe1b8ed5e299fc485f61R89-R111)`)

**Favicon and manifest support:**

* Added a comprehensive favicon HTML snippet (`HTML_SNIPPET.txt`), a browser configuration XML (`browserconfig.xml`), and a robots.txt file to the `public` directory, improving cross-platform icon and SEO support. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5901fe0e7e262d862958606278e12f572b92383396c64442664f612a195983ceR1-R32)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-825bfd9170034ae5d6e73a8505b639a179d1b0e13e3e6c1efbc147e8eeeba21fR1-R9)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5f811c77bc921ff42910051d6a5642fb452f7f16e70cbec6c1c5ab9e9a3d92bdR1-R11)`)
* Updated `site.webmanifest` with proper app name, icons, and color values for improved PWA support. (`[app/public/site.webmanifestL1-R19](diffhunk://#diff-cce7bcf9ccccf000f15b448490f7defd806337bd602c9685eb59e94fcaa75166L1-R19)`)

**Content reading UI/UX improvements:**

* Enhanced `ReadingCore` and `ReadingUI` components to support updating the current section index via a new `updateCurrentIndex` prop, improving section tracking as users read. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9141afeee3560bace8c338ef5ae3e42a392c8fe42f88d573f271c5d1db3711c3R39)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9141afeee3560bace8c338ef5ae3e42a392c8fe42f88d573f271c5d1db3711c3R90)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9141afeee3560bace8c338ef5ae3e42a392c8fe42f88d573f271c5d1db3711c3R150-R152)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3f1fff7f8a83c2178ac70139c1f1d60ccaf120d63555d965f3e031d15626f03dR20)`, `[[5]](diffhunk://#diff-3f1fff7f8a83c2178ac70139c1f1d60ccaf120d63555d965f3e031d15626f03dR53)`, `[[6]](diffhunk://#diff-3f1fff7f8a83c2178ac70139c1f1d60ccaf120d63555d965f3e031d15626f03dR77)`)
* Improved the `SectionsSheet` table of contents component with a smooth exit animation by tracking mount state with `shouldRender`, providing a better user experience when closing the menu. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a30c22a9bc0515a40b52c87162d440e838037956042f4e0045f43de24dae7f25L1-R1)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a30c22a9bc0515a40b52c87162d440e838037956042f4e0045f43de24dae7f25R71-R84)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a30c22a9bc0515a40b52c87162d440e838037956042f4e0045f43de24dae7f25R114-R117)`)

body:
Fixes #22

## Summary
Addresses all 7 categories of issues identified by CodeRabbit in PR #19 (Icon Library Generator). Changes improve storage safety, SSR compatibility, accessibility, state management, security, and data integrity.

## Changes

### High Priority
- **Storage safety** (deleteIcon): Delete storage before DB record to prevent orphaned blobs
- **Schema mismatch**: Documented session-only style settings (bowing, randomize, pencilFilter) that reset on page reload

### Medium Priority
- **SSR compatibility**: Added browser environment guard to svgToExcalidrawElements
- **Accessibility**:

  - Added aria-label to library name input
- **State management**: Include isSaving in isBusy check to prevent operations during save
- **Security**: Validate SVG before export processing (skip invalid, don't crash)

### Low Priority
- **Data integrity**:
  - Two-phase validation in reorderIcons (validate all, then patch all)
  - ZIP filename deduplication (append -1, -2 on collision)

## Verification
- ✅ `bun run build` passes without SSR errors
- ✅ TypeScript compilation clean
- ✅ LSP diagnostics clean on all modified files
- ✅ All 7 CodeRabbit issue categories addressed

body:
The `NewAlertModel()` signature expects `time.Duration`, but `NewAlertCmd` was [incorrectly multiplying `m.duration` by `time.Second`](https://github.com/DaltonSW/BubbleUp/pull/4/changes/32eb771a910ed4399741cff2360de5702c5bcf78#diff-0ac0ad254c0aec99dc10fb85024c37e97ada12832a9c2b9256bdbe3573f946e8R154), causing timeouts passed as a `time.Duration` vs. as an `int` to be wrong

Changes:
- `alert.go`: Removed `time.Second` multiplication from `NewAlertCmd()` 
- `model.go`: Added default case to continue ticking on non-alert messages
- `README.md`: Updated all examples to use `N*time.Second` syntax
- `examples/example_main.go`: Updated to use `10*time.Second`

**BREAKING CHANGE** _(since PR #4):_ Code passing raw integers (e.g., `10`) will now correctly receive `10 nanoseconds` instead of incorrectly receiving `10 seconds`. Update code to use proper `time.Duration` values e.g., `10*time.Second`.

This change views the parameter type of `time.Duration` as authoritative and makes its use reflect the intent of the data type rather than treat it as if it were an int.

body:
## Summary
This PR addresses critical race conditions in estimate status updates, corrects financial metric terminology from "gross margin" to "projected margin", and improves KPI definition validation and semantic mappings.

## Key Changes

### Estimate Status Updates (EstimateStatusActions.tsx)
- **Race condition fix**: Fetch fresh database status instead of relying on stale props to prevent concurrent update conflicts
- **No-op prevention**: Guard against redundant status transitions with user feedback
- **Simplified approval flow**: Consolidate status + is_current_version updates into single write operation
- **Safe un-approval**: Only revert project status to 'quoted' if currently in 'in_progress' or 'approved' states, preventing overwrites of projects that have progressed further (e.g., 'complete')
- **Improved error handling**: Reorganized status update logic with clearer separation of approval vs. simple transitions

### Financial Metrics Terminology
- Renamed `activeGrossMargin` → `activeProjectedMargin` and `activeGrossMarginPercent` → `activeProjectedMarginPercent` across Dashboard, ProjectStatusCard, and WorkOrderStatusCard components
- Updated KPI definitions to clarify "projected margin" uses estimated costs as denominator, distinct from "actual margin" which uses contracted amount

### KPI Definitions & Validation (lib/kpi-definitions/)
- **Semantic mappings**: Added "estimated hours" concept; clarified "hours" refers to actual work hours; removed "cushion" alias from contingency
- **Business benchmarks**: Updated metric names for consistency (e.g., `billing_progress_percent` → `budget_utilization_percent`)
- **Evaluation logic**: Improved `evaluateMetric()` to correctly handle metrics where low values are bad (margin, billing) vs. high values are bad (cost variance, contingency)
- **Field path validation**: Added checks for valid table.column format in KPI definitions
- **Related KPI references**: Added validation to ensure relatedTo references point to valid KPI IDs
- **Business rules**: Clarified preference for reporting.project_financials view over manual calculations

### Data Integrity & Validation
- **Expense splits**: Added validation for minimum split count (≥2) and positive amounts; guard against division by zero
- **Revenue splits**: Enhanced validation with negative/zero amount checks; improved rollback logic to restore original project_id on failure; reordered operations to delete splits after parent update for better recovery
- **Time entry validation**: Changed error handling to return `hasOverlap: true` on validation failures, preventing potentially overlapping entries from being created

### Profit Calculations
- Fixed chronological sorting in `calculateProfitTrends()` to properly order months by index rather than string comparison

### Dashboard Metrics
- Updated active project count filter to include only 'in_progress' and 'approved' statuses (removed 'quoted') for consistency with financial metrics calculations

## Notable Implementation Details
- Fresh status fetches use database values to prevent race conditions in concurrent scenarios
- Safe un-approval checks project status before reverting to prevent data loss
- KPI validation now catches orphaned references and inconsistent field paths
- Improved error recovery in split operations by reordering database operations

## Summary
This PR introduces a completely isolated capital data extraction module (`capital_extractor.py`) that extracts capital information (Report Type 5) from the BCB's IFDATA API. The module operates independently with its own cache system and does not impact the existing main extraction workflow.

## Key Changes

- **New module**: `utils/capital_extractor.py` - Standalone capital data extraction with:
  - Independent HTTP fetching with retry/backoff logic
  - Period-based data processing (quarterly: 03, 06, 09, 12)
  - Automatic field mapping (16 capital-related metrics)
  - Incremental cache management with progressive saving
  - Isolated logging configuration

- **Separate cache system**: 
  - `data/capital_cache.pkl` - Stores extracted capital data by period
  - `data/capital_cache_info.txt` - Metadata about cache state
  - No interference with existing `dados_cache.pkl`

- **UI integration** in `app1.py`:
  - New "extrair capital" section with period selection (2015-2027)
  - Real-time progress tracking and status updates
  - Cache info display (number of periods, file size, last update)
  - Field extraction details in expandable section
  - Incremental save callbacks during processing

- **Updated `.gitignore`**: Added capital cache files to ignore list

## Implementation Details

- **Isolation**: Module imports only standard libraries + pandas/requests, no dependencies on `ifdata_extractor.py`
- **Field mapping**: 16 capital metrics mapped from API names to user-friendly names (e.g., "Índice de Basileia" → "Índice de Basileia")
- **Error handling**: Graceful degradation with emergency saves on extraction failures
- **Rate limiting**: 1.5s delay between API calls to respect service limits
- **Incremental processing**: Supports progressive saving every N periods to prevent data loss
- **Alias support**: Respects institution name aliases from main workflow when available

## Testing Recommendations

- Verify capital cache is created independently without affecting main cache
- Test period selection and extraction with various date ranges
- Confirm incremental saves work correctly
- Validate field mapping against API responses

body:
Users can now tap anywhere on the page to register BPM taps, not just the "Tap" button.

## Changes

- Added document-level click listener that calls `handleTap()` on any click
- Excluded `.controls` and `.graph-container` to preserve interactive elements (slider, reset button, graph tooltips)
- Removed redundant `onClick` from Tap button (now handled by document listener)
- Updated hint text to indicate click-anywhere capability

## Implementation

```javascript
useEffect(() => {
    const handleClick = (e) => {
        const target = e.target;
        if (target.closest('.controls') || target.closest('.graph-container')) {
            return;
        }
        handleTap();
    };
    document.addEventListener('click', handleClick);
    return () => document.removeEventListener('click', handleClick);
}, [handleTap]);
```

Keyboard shortcuts (Space, Enter, T) continue to work as before.

author: thirteenflt
body:
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-issues/issues/405

### Problem

When using the Responses API endpoint, the `engine.messages` telemetry event was receiving an empty `messagesJson` array (`[]`). This happened because:

- **Chat Completions API** uses `request.messages` field
- **Responses API** uses `request.input` field instead

The telemetry logging code in `_fetchWithInstrumentation` was only checking `request.messages`, which is empty for Responses API requests.

### Solution

Updated the `.finally()` block in `chatMLFetcher.ts` to detect when `request.messages` is empty and `request.input` exists. In this case, it converts the Responses API input to `CAPIChatMessage[]` format using:

1. `responseApiInputToRawMessagesForLogging()` - converts Responses API input to `Raw.ChatMessage[]`
2. `rawMessageToCAPI()` - converts each raw message to `CAPIChatMessage`

### Changes

- `src/extension/prompt/node/chatMLFetcher.ts`
  - Added imports for `responseApiInputToRawMessagesForLogging` and `rawMessageToCAPI`
  - Updated `.finally()` block to handle Responses API input conversion with error handling

- `src/extension/prompt/node/test/chatMLFetcherRetry.spec.ts`
  - Added unit test to verify Responses API input is converted to messages for telemetry

### Testing

- Added unit test: `converts Responses API input to messages for telemetry`
- All 13 tests pass in `chatMLFetcherRetry.spec.ts`

Estas mejoras están diseñadas para mejorar la automatización, la eficiencia operativa y la gestión proactiva de proveedores. Además, se mejoró el mdulo de usarios, roles y permisos.

* Se añadió `MonitorearStockCommand` (`stock:monitorear`), que detecta productos que necesitan reabastecimiento, genera solicitudes de compra automáticamente y puede enviarlas a los proveedores por correo electrónico o WhatsApp. También marca solicitudes de cotización vencidas, consolidando la automatización de stock y compras en un solo comando.

author: cmm25
body:
This pull request introduces user authentication to the article agent API and ensures all article-related actions are logged with user context. The main changes include requiring a valid user session for article agent actions, passing the user's access token from the frontend, and updating trace logging to associate actions with the correct user. Additionally, a fallback article is shown if no session exists, and a minor UI change removes the navigation menu from the homepage.

**Authentication and API security:**

* The `article-agent-proxy` API now requires authentication: it checks for a valid user session and returns a 401 Unauthorized response if none is found. (`swahili/app/api/article-agent-proxy/route.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-81eff889a6404823e7d45302875429ea93587cd813385d7c1297a898bb732300R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-81eff889a6404823e7d45302875429ea93587cd813385d7c1297a898bb732300R122-R129)
* The frontend (`DailyArticleFeature`) retrieves the user's access token from Supabase and includes it in the `Authorization` header for API requests. If no session is found, it displays a fallback article instead of making the request. (`swahili/components/article/DailyArticleFeature.tsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d0aa85bc3491c6e6c775bdc25fd394ee6cb558cfcba2989994631311e0dffcafR7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d0aa85bc3491c6e6c775bdc25fd394ee6cb558cfcba2989994631311e0dffcafR45-R60)

**Trace logging improvements:**

* All calls to `logTrace` now include the authenticated user's ID, allowing for better tracking of user actions. (`swahili/app/api/article-agent-proxy/route.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-81eff889a6404823e7d45302875429ea93587cd813385d7c1297a898bb732300R159) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-81eff889a6404823e7d45302875429ea93587cd813385d7c1297a898bb732300R189) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-81eff889a6404823e7d45302875429ea93587cd813385d7c1297a898bb732300R223) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-81eff889a6404823e7d45302875429ea93587cd813385d7c1297a898bb732300R262) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-81eff889a6404823e7d45302875429ea93587cd813385d7c1297a898bb732300R288)
* The backend logging function now falls back to a default trace user ID if no user is provided, ensuring trace logs are not skipped unnecessarily. (`swahili/lib/opik.ts`)

**UI update:**

* The navigation menu has been removed from the homepage for a cleaner look. (`swahili/app/page.tsx`)…yArticleFeature to include access token in API requests. Update logging to ensure userId is captured for better traceability in Supabase logs.

author: alexwelcing
body:
## Summary

Transform the skills-based framework into a living agent-based marketing agency called "High Era." This restructures how users interact with the system—instead of loading individual skills, users now spawn specialized AI agents (Director, Strategist, Copywriter, Editor, Optimizer, Analyst) that orchestrate work together.

## Key Changes

- **Renamed and repositioned**: Changed from "Copy & Marketing Agency" to "High Era: Marketing Agency" with agent-first architecture
- **Created agent system**: Added 6 specialized agent definitions with distinct personalities and responsibilities:
  - `Director` - Orchestrates projects and ensures delivery
  - `Strategist` - Positioning, psychology, competitive analysis
  - `Copywriter` - Headlines, pages, emails, ads
  - `Editor` - Polish, consistency, quality gate
  - `Optimizer` - CRO, page structure, conversion
  - `Analyst` - Measurement, tracking, data
- **Added communication protocols**: Structured handoff, review, escalation, and sync protocols for agent-to-agent communication
- **Implemented agency board**: Live state tracking via `status.json`, `active.json`, and `inbox.json` for project and agent status
- **Created spawn entry points**: Quick-start patterns (`brief.md`, `write.md`, `audit.md`, `optimize.md`, `strategy.md`) for common workflows
- **Updated documentation**: Rewrote main README to emphasize agent-based workflows instead of skill loading
- **Added AGENCY.md**: New file explaining the agency system and how agents work together

## Implementation Details

- Agents have distinct personalities and push back when something's off-strategy
- Work flows through explicit handoff protocol with context preservation
- Director owns accountability and orchestrates team assembly
- Each agent draws from the existing 23-skill library but applies them through their specialized lens
- Board system enables tracking of active projects, agent availability, and pending requests
- Protocols ensure agents can work autonomously while maintaining coordination

## Backward Compatibility

The underlying skills library remains unchanged—agents simply provide a new interface layer for accessing and applying them. Users can still load skills directly if needed.

# Enhanced Code Quality and Testing Infrastructure

I've completed several improvements to enhance code quality, testing infrastructure, and maintainability:

## Completed Tasks:

### Testing Infrastructure Improvements
- Added comprehensive test fixtures in `conftest.py` including:
  - State configurations for Texas and Oklahoma
  - Sample records for contributions, expenditures, and filers
  - Database session fixtures (mock and in-memory SQLite)
  - Field library fixtures and temporary file fixtures
  - Validation test fixtures and custom pytest markers

### Code Quality Enhancements
- Implemented code coverage threshold of 70% in CI workflow
- Fixed type alias syntax in `abc_validation.py` using proper `Union` type
- Replaced `ic()` debug calls with structured logging throughout the codebase

### New Utilities
- Created `dataframe_utils.py` with reusable functions:
  - `align_columns()` - Ensures DataFrame has all required columns
  - `get_all_columns_from_files()` - Gets union of columns from parquet files
  - `get_columns_by_suffix()/get_columns_by_prefix()` - Filters columns by naming patterns
  - `consolidate_parquet_files()` - Consolidates multiple files with schema alignment
  - `cast_columns_by_suffix()` - Casts columns based on suffix patterns

### Improved Logging
- Enhanced `Logger` class to support structured logging with `extra` parameter
- Standardized logging format for better traceability

### Code Organization
- Cleaned up `main.py` by moving experimental code to `scripts/analysis/experiments.py`
- Added proper module docstrings and clear entry points
- Created clean utility functions like `load_texas_dataframes()`, `search_contributions()`, and `search_expenditures()`

### Documentation
- Added `CLAUDE.md` with comprehensive project documentation for AI assistants
- Improved docstrings throughout the codebase

All tests in `app/tests/` pass successfully with the new changes.

body:
### Ticket
[Link to Github Issue](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/issues/5951)

### Problem description
Commute Patterns for Softmax with Reshape.
This commit adds changes to commute upwards and downwards the reshape op through the softmax using stride and reduction length of the softmax dimension.

### What's changed
Added Commute Patterns for Softmax with Reshape. Now,  Inverse TensorManipulation Ops like Reshape can be folded by commuting them upwards or downwards through the graph, improving the performance.

For eg, swin model as it has 24 softmax-es each surrounded by two reshapes, which could be folded away.

```
%345 = "ttnn.reshape"(%344)  tensor<1083x49x49xbf16> -> tensor<361x3x49x49xbf16>
%346 = "ttnn.softmax"(%345) <{dimension = 3 : si32, numericStable = true}> 
%347 = "ttnn.reshape"(%346)  tensor<361x3x49x49xbf16> -> tensor<1083x49x49xbf16>
```

which would be rewritten with this commute as just:

```
%346 = "ttnn.softmax"(%345) <{dimension = 2 : si32, numericStable = true}>
```

### Notes

#### Update Softmax Dimension with Stride and reduction Length

Maps a softmax axis across a reshape by matching both: 
1. The reduction length of the axis, and 
2. Its contiguous stride.

```
     Consider a Tensor with shape = [2, 3, 4]
       i=0,j=0,k=0
       i=0,j=0,k=1
       i=0,j=0,k=2
       i=0,j=0,k=3
       i=0,j=1,k=0
       ...
     strides = [3*4, 4, 1]

Example 1 (Valid commute):
       Input shape      = [2, 3, 4]
       Softmax dim      = 2  (stride = 1, reduction length = 4)
       Reshape          = [6, 4]
The new softmax dim is 1, since output dim 1 still has stride = 1 and reduction length = 4.
     
Example 2 (Invalid Commute)
       Input shape      = [2, 3, 4]
       Softmax dim      = 1  (stride = 4, reduction length = 3)
       Reshape          = [2, 12]
output strides = [12, 1],  Hence, we can't apply softmax because no dimension in output has stride 4 and reduction len = 3
```

#### Upwards

```
   %0 = softmax(%arg0 : tensor<1x160x160x128xbf16>) <{dimension = 3}>
   %1 = reshape(%0) <{shape = [1 : i32, 25600 : i32, 128 : i32]}>
to
   %0 = reshape(%arg0 : tensor<1x160x160x128xbf16>) <{shape = [1 : i32, 25600 : i32, 128 : i32]}>
   %1 = softmax(%0) <{dimension = 2}>
```


#### Downwards
```
   %0 = reshape(%arg0 : tensor<1x160x160x128xbf16>) <{shape = [1 : i32, 25600 : i32, 128 : i32]}>
   %1 = softmax(%0) <{dimension = 2}>
 
to
   
   %0 = softmax(%arg0 : tensor<1x160x160x128xbf16>) <{dimension = 3}>
   %1 = reshape(%0) <{shape = [1 : i32, 25600 : i32, 128 : i32]}>
```

<!-- 이 PR의 전체적인 변경 내용을 한두 문장으로 요약해주세요. 예시: "로그인 기능 오류를 수정했습니다." -->
iOS 26에서 UIScreen.main이 deprecated 되면서 발생한 경고를 제거하기 위해,   
마커/오버레이 이미지 렌더링 시 전역 화면 대신 실제 렌더링 컨텍스트의 displayScale을 주입하도록 구조를 변경했습니다.

## 🔨 What  
<!-- 
1. 어떤 작업(수정, 추가, 삭제 등)을 했는지 구체적으로 작성해주세요. 예시: "로그인 API 에러 처리 로직 추가, 로그인 UI 버튼 위치 조정"
2. UI 변경 등 시각적으로 확인이 필요한 경우, 아래에 스크린샷이나 캡처 이미지를 첨부해주세요.
-->
1.	MarkerImageCache(및 관련 캐시)의 이미지 생성 API를 scale 주입 방식으로 변경 (image(for:scale:), userLocationImage(..., scale:), selectedPinImage(..., scale:))
2.	캐시 키에 scale을 포함해, 서로 다른 화면 스케일(멀티 윈도우/외부 디스플레이 등)에서 잘못된 이미지 재사용을 방지
3.	지도 마커를 생성/갱신하는 매니저 및 뷰(Coordinator)들에서 mapView.window?.windowScene?.screen.scale 또는 traitCollection.displayScale로 scale을 계산해 캐시에 전달
  - InfrastructureMarkerManager, CaseLocationMarkerManager, TrackingNaverMapView, OverviewNaverMapView 등 연쇄 수정

## 👀 Review Notes  
<!-- 리뷰어에게 요청하거나 참고해야 할 사항을 작성해주세요. 예시: "중점적으로 봐줬으면 하는 부분, 테스트 방법, 논의가 필요한 부분 등" -->
- displayScale 계산은 windowScene.screen.scale 우선, traitCollection.displayScale 폴백으로 통일했습니다. (window가 nil인 타이밍 고려)
- 변경된 cache API 호출부들이 모두 scale을 전달하는지 확인 부탁드립니다. (특히 Task 내부에서 marker icon 갱신하는 부분)
- 멀티 씬/외부 디스플레이 환경에서 scale이 달라질 수 있어, 캐시 키에 scale 포함 로직이 의도대로 동작하는지 중점 리뷰 부탁드립니다.

## Canada Child Benefit (CCB) Calculator Implementation

This PR adds a comprehensive Canada Child Benefit (CCB) calculator to TaxSyncForDrivers, providing families with children under 18 the ability to estimate their federal tax-free monthly payments.

### 🎯 What's New

**✅ Core Calculator (`canada-child-benefit-calculator.js`)**
- `calculateCCB()` - Main calculation with 2-phase income reduction
- `estimateCCBEligibility()` - Quick eligibility check
- `calculateAFNI()` - Adjusted Family Net Income calculator
- 2026 CCB rates: $7,787/year (under 6), $6,570/year (6-17)
- Child Disability Benefit (CDB) support: $3,322/year supplement
- Income-tested phase-out starting at $35,000
- **Age validation**: Filters children aged 18+ or with invalid ages

**✅ Comprehensive Test Suite (22 tests, all passing)**
- Low income scenarios (full benefit)
- Income phase-out calculations (2 phases)
- Disability supplement (CDB)
- Edge cases (empty children, very high income)
- AFNI calculations
- **Age validation tests**: Invalid ages (18+, negative)
- Test coverage: 100%

**✅ UI Integration**
- New tab in navigation: 🇨🇦 Canada Child Benefit
- Dynamic child input system (add/remove children)
- Real-time calculation with detailed breakdown
- Mobile-responsive design

**✅ Bilingual Support**

- EN: "Canada Child Benefit"
- FR: "Allocation canadienne pour enfants"

**✅ Documentation**

### 📸 Screenshots

![CCB Calculator Form](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b730e40-0402-4db2-a357-663450c917a7)

- Child #2 (6-17): $6,570 base

### ✅ Test Results

Pass: 1000
Fail: 1 (unrelated email-integration test)
CCB Tests: 22/22 passing ✅
```

### 📋 Implementation Details

**Features:**

- Per-child calculations with age-based rates

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Objective

Add **Canada Child Benefit (CCB)** calculator to support Canadian families with children under 18. This is a critical federal benefit that provides up to **$7,787/year per child under 6** and **$6,570/year per child 6-17**.

---

## Background

The Canada Child Benefit is:
- **Tax-free monthly payment** for families with children under 18
- **Income-tested** - reduces as family net income increases
- **Indexed annually** - 2026 rates updated
- **Universal** - available in all provinces/territories
- **One of the largest federal benefits** affecting millions of Canadian families

---

## Requirements

### 1. **Create `canada-child-benefit-calculator.js`**

#### **CCB Payment Amounts (2026):**
```javascript
export const CCB_RATES_2026 = {
  // Base amounts per child
  baseAmountUnder6: 7787,      // Per child under 6 years
  baseAmount6to17: 6570,        // Per child 6-17 years
  
  // Phase-out thresholds
  phaseOut1Start: 35000,        // Income where reduction begins
  phaseOut1Rate: 0.07,          // 7% reduction on income over $35,000
  phaseOut1Limit: 73000,        // Income where phase 2 begins
  
  phaseOut2Rate: 0.032,         // 3.2% additional reduction over $73,000
  
  // Disability supplement
  childDisabilityBenefit: 3322, // Annual CDB amount per eligible child
  cdbPhaseOutStart: 73000,
  cdbPhaseOutRate: 0.032,
};
```

#### **Core Functions:**

```javascript
/**
 * Calculate Canada Child Benefit for a family
 * @param {number} familyNetIncome - Adjusted family net income
 * @param {Array} children - Array of child objects
 * @param {number} children[].age - Child's age
 * @param {boolean} children[].hasDisability - Whether child is eligible for CDB
 * @returns {Object} CCB calculation
 */
export function calculateCCB(familyNetIncome, children) {
  // Validate inputs
  if (!Array.isArray(children) || children.length === 0) {
    return {
      totalAnnualCCB: 0,
      monthlyPayment: 0,
      childrenUnder6: 0,
      children6to17: 0,
      baseAmount: 0,
      reductionAmount: 0,
      disabilitySupplement: 0,
      breakdown: [],
    };
  }
  
  let baseAmount = 0;
  let disabilitySupplement = 0;
  const breakdown = [];
  
  // Calculate base amounts per child
  children.forEach((child, index) => {
    const childBase = child.age < 6 
      ? CCB_RATES_2026.baseAmountUnder6 
      : CCB_RATES_2026.baseAmount6to17;
    
    baseAmount += childBase;
    
    // Add disability supplement if eligible
    if (child.hasDisability) {
      disabilitySupplement += CCB_RATES_2026.childDisabilityBenefit;
    }
    
    breakdown.push({
      childNumber: index + 1,
      age: child.age,
      ageGroup: child.age < 6 ? 'Under 6' : '6-17',
      baseAmount: childBase,
      hasDisability: child.hasDisability || false,
      disabilitySupplement: child.hasDisability ? CCB_RATES_2026.childDisabilityBenefit : 0,
    });
  });
  
  // Calculate income-tested reduction
  let reductionAmount = 0;
  
  if (familyNetIncome > CCB_RATES_2026.phaseOut1Start) {
    const phase1Income = Math.min(
      familyNetIncome - CCB_RATES_2026.phaseOut1Start,
      CCB_RATES_2026.phaseOut1Limit - CCB_RATES_2026.phaseOut1Start
    );
    reductionAmount += phase1Income * CCB_RATES_2026.phaseOut1Rate * children.length;
  }
  
  if (familyNetIncome > CCB_RATES_2026.phaseOut1Limit) {
    const phase2Income = familyNetIncome - CCB_RATES_2026.phaseOut1Limit;
    reductionAmount += phase2Income * CCB_RATES_2026.phaseOut2Rate * children.length;
  }
  
  // Reduce disability supplement separately
  let disabilityReduction = 0;
  if (familyNetIncome > CCB_RATES_2026.cdbPhaseOutStart && disabilitySupplement > 0) {
    const excessIncome = familyNetIncome - CCB_RATES_2026.cdbPhaseOutStart;
    const childrenWithDisability = children.filter(c => c.hasDisability).length;
    disabilityReduction = Math.min(
      excessIncome * CCB_RATES_2026.cdbPhaseOutRate * childrenWithDisability,
      disabilitySupplement
    );
  }
  
  // Calculate final amounts
  const totalAnnualCCB = Math.max(0, baseAmount - reductionAmount + disabilitySupplement - disabilityReduction);
  const monthlyPayment = totalAnnualCCB / 12;
  
  return {
    totalAnnualCCB: Math.round(totalAnnualCCB * 100) / 100,
    monthlyPayment: Math.round(monthlyPayment * 100) / 100,
    childrenUnder6: children.filter(c => c.age < 6).length,
    children6to17: children.filter(c => c.age >= 6 && c.age <= 17).length,
    totalChildren: children.length,

## 🎯 Objetivo
Este PR implementa os adaptadores de entrada (Controllers) e as rotas HTTP para a entidade [ProblemReport](cci:2://file:///c:/Users/levan/Reposit%C3%B3rios/EcoRota-PI_IV/backend/src/presentation/controllers/ProblemReportController.ts:31:0-110:1), permitindo que cidadãos reportem incidentes de coleta e que administradores gerenciem a resolução desses problemas.

## 🛠️ Mudanças Realizadas

### Camada de Presentation
- **ProblemReportController.ts**: Criação do controlador de relatos.
    - Implementação de validações com **Zod**, garantindo que campos como `description`, `problemType` e `subscriberId` estejam corretos.
    - Método específico [resolve](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/levan/Reposit%C3%B3rios/EcoRota-PI_IV/backend/src/presentation/controllers/ProblemReportController.ts:70:4-85:5) para tratar a transição de status do problema.
    - Orquestração dos casos de uso: Report, List, Resolve, Update e Delete.
- **problemReportRoutes.ts**: Configuração das rotas e injeção de dependências.
    - **POST /problem-reports**: Rota pública para facilitar o acesso do cidadão.
    - **Rotas Administrativas**: Todas as demais operações (Listagem, Resolução, Edição, Exclusão) são protegidas pelo middleware `ensureAuthenticated`.

### Integração
- **app.ts**: Registro do módulo de rotas de [ProblemReport](cci:2://file:///c:/Users/levan/Reposit%C3%B3rios/EcoRota-PI_IV/backend/src/presentation/controllers/ProblemReportController.ts:31:0-110:1) no servidor Express.

## 🛣️ Novos Endpoints

| Método | Rota | Descrição | Autenticação |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| POST | `/problem-reports` | Criação de um novo relato | Não |
| GET | `/problem-reports` | Listagem de relatos (filtros por status/protocolo) | Sim (Admin) |
| PATCH | `/problem-reports/:id/resolve` | Resolução do problema | Sim (Admin) |
| PUT | `/problem-reports/:id` | Atualização do relato | Sim (Admin) |
| DELETE | `/problem-reports/:id` | Exclusão do relato | Sim (Admin) |

## ✅ Verificação (DoD)
- [x] Fluxo de criação e resolução validado.
- [x] Proteção de rotas administrativas ativa (retorno 401 sem token).
- [x] Validação de entrada rigorosa (Zod) impedindo dados inválidos.
- [x] Injeção de dependência correta para casos de uso complexos (ex: [UpdateProblemReportUseCase](cci:2://file:///c:/Users/levan/Reposit%C3%B3rios/EcoRota-PI_IV/backend/src/application/use-cases/problem-report/UpdateProblemReportUseCase.ts:11:0-54:1)).
- [x] Build do projeto concluído com sucesso (`npm run build`).

body:
### Motivation
- Provide an in-browser admin workflow so authorized owners can upload report PDFs and metadata without exposing the Supabase service role key in the browser. 
- Reuse Supabase Google sign-in and whitelist specific emails so uploads are restricted to allowed admins. 
- Proxy report PDFs through the app so the Supabase storage URL is not exposed to site visitors. 

### Description
- Add a client admin page at `app/system/page.tsx` that implements Google sign-in via Supabase, stores a short-lived session in `localStorage`, refreshes tokens, and displays a form for report metadata and a PDF upload. 
- Add a secure server API route at `app/api/system/reports/route.ts` that validates the Supabase session via `/auth/v1/user`, checks `SYSTEM_ALLOWED_EMAILS`, accepts multipart form uploads, uploads the PDF to Supabase Storage using the service role key, and inserts a row into `research_reports` via the Supabase REST endpoint. 
- Add a storage proxy route at `app/api/research/report-pdf/[slug]/route.ts` and update the report viewer to load `/api/research/report-pdf/<slug>` so PDF URLs are not exposed directly. 
- Update `docs/research-reports.md` to document the `/system` workflow and list required environment variables (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `REPORTS_BUCKET`, `SYSTEM_ALLOWED_EMAILS`). 

### Testing
- Started the dev server with `pnpm dev --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000`, which compiled the app (Google Fonts downloads warned but fell back) and surfaced an initial runtime error when client env vars were missing; the client page was then hardened to guard missing envs. 
- Re-ran the dev server and confirmed it starts and serves the new routes when the required env vars are present. 
- Attempted an automated Playwright screenshot of `/system`, but the headless Chromium process crashed (SIGSEGV) in this environment and the browser-based capture failed; no further integration tests were executed.

body: Based on this blog post https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/on-policy-distillation/ -- figured Arctic Training would be an appropriate place to have this feature. Training validated with GSM8K dataset on Qwen3-1.7B model using Qwen3-8B teacher. Lower teacher perplexity means teacher is less surprised by the student's answer. Higher teacher logprob means teacher agrees with the student's answer. Lower reverse KL means student's answers converge to teacher's. Student's perplexity initially jumped up, meaning it's learning, and slowly ramped down, meaning it's getting more confident along the training progress. Full dashboard: https://snowflake.wandb.io/thongnguyen/on-policy-distillation-gsm8k/runs/zuwzrd11?nw=nwuserthongnguyen Once this PR is in we can make the claim ArcticTraining supports RL :)

author: panaresium
body:
- Modified `app_factory.py` to handle database connection failures gracefully at runtime.
  - Implemented a reconnect attempt on user-initiated requests (login, refresh, API calls) when `DB_CONNECTION_FAILED` is set.
  - If reconnection succeeds, the failure flag is cleared, restoring normal application function.
  - If reconnection fails, requests are redirected to `ui.serve_login` (UI) or return a 503 JSON (API), with static assets explicitly permitted to ensure the login page renders.
- Updated `auth.py` to prevent `load_user` from crashing when the DB is offline by returning `None`.
- Updated `routes/ui.py` to flash the specific database error message on the login screen.
- Bypassed the `/setup` redirect when the DB is offline to prevent crash loops.

author: michaelfutol
body:
### Motivation
- Provide the second half (items 51–100) of Mock Exam 1 so the backend can serve a full 100-item mock exam without runtime generation. 
- Make the dataset directly importable by the backend storage layer and accessible to clients via a simple retrieval endpoint. 

### Description
- Added the Part B JSON data file at `backend/data/mock_exam1_part_b.json` containing items `MOCK1-051`…`MOCK1-100`. 
- Wired Part B into storage by adding `MOCK_EXAM1_PART_B_PATH` and a loader function `load_mock_exam1_part_b()` in `backend/app/storage.py`. 
- Exposed a new API route `GET /mock-exams/1/part-b` in `backend/app/main.py` that returns `list[MockQuestion]`. 
- Fixed a JSON parsing bug in one item where unescaped double-quotes (inches) caused a parse error by escaping the quotes (`2\" x 8\" x 8'.`).

### Testing
- Validated the Part B payload syntax with `python -m json.tool backend/data/mock_exam1_part_b.json`, which initially failed and then succeeded after the quoting fix. 
- Confirmed the new loader and route exist in `backend/app/storage.py` and `backend/app/main.py` by static inspection (no import-time schema errors observed during local validation).

author: maduranga98
body:
## Summary
This PR implements a comprehensive redesign of the homepage with a new brand design system, updated color palette, and restructured page sections for improved clarity and user experience.

## Key Changes

### Brand Design System
- Introduced comprehensive CSS variables for primary colors (blue-900, blue-600, cyan-500), neutrals, and status colors
- Updated primary brand color from `#2563eb` to `#1E3A8A` (darker blue) throughout the application
- Maintained legacy color aliases for backward compatibility
- Updated all gradients, shadows, and animations to use the new color system

### Homepage Restructuring
- **Removed sections**: ServicesSection, ApproachSection, AboutSection, WhyChooseUsSection, FAQSection, BlogPreviewSection
- **Added sections**: 
  - `WhoWeAreSection` - New company introduction with image and description
  - `WhatWeDoSection` - Service offerings with icons and detailed explanation
  - `InnovationSection` - Showcase of flagship products (BPRS, GymNex) with status badges
  - `CTASection` - New call-to-action section with background image and consultation button
- **Reorganized flow**: Cleaner narrative from Hero → Who We Are → What We Do → Products → Industries → Innovation → CTA → Contact

### Hero Section Redesign
- Changed from full-screen gradient overlay to subtle dark overlay with background image
- Replaced statistics bar with prominent white card containing company name and value proposition
- Simplified CTA to single "Read More" button linking to about section
- Reduced height to 70vh for better pacing
- Removed decorative blob animations for cleaner aesthetic

### Component Updates
- **Navbar**: Updated all color references to use new blue-900 primary color
- **ContactSection**: Updated heading color and button styling to match new brand
- **ProductsSection**: Simplified to 3-column grid layout with consistent card design
- **IndustriesSection**: Redesigned with 2-column layout (image + text) instead of badge grid

### Color Palette Updates
- Primary buttons changed from blue-600 to blue-900
- Accent colors updated to cyan-500 for secondary CTAs
- All hover states and transitions updated consistently
- Shadow colors adjusted to use new primary blue

## Implementation Details
- All smooth scroll navigation preserved with proper offset calculations
- Maintained responsive design across mobile, tablet, and desktop
- Used existing AnimatedSection component for consistent animations
- Preserved accessibility and semantic HTML structure
- Updated Tailwind color references throughout (e.g., `text-blue-600` → `text-blue-900`)

## Visual Impact
The redesign creates a more professional, focused brand presence with:
- Clearer information hierarchy
- Reduced cognitive load through streamlined sections
- Stronger visual identity with consistent color system
- Improved mobile responsiveness with better spacing

author: gberg01
body:
### Motivation

- Establish a single canonical migration workflow (Prisma) for ongoing schema changes and developer ergonomics. 
- Provide a runnable local DB scaffold and seed data to make ingestion and API development easier. 
- Surface consistent API error payloads and centralize logging to simplify frontend error handling and server debugging. 

### Description

- Add Prisma as a dependency and helper scripts in `packages/db/package.json` and provide a `packages/db/.env.example` with `DATABASE_URL` to standardize local setup. 
- Introduce a full DB package including `migrations/001_init.sql`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, `seed.sql`, a connection helper `packages/db/src/client.ts`, and query helpers under `packages/db/src/queries/*`. 
- Scaffold a minimal Next.js `apps/web` app with Route Handlers for `episodes`, `contestants`, and `performances`, plus `mock-data`, a small `logError` helper, and configuration files (`next.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `next-env.d.ts`). 
- Add shared API types in `packages/shared/src/api.ts` to standardize `ApiResponse` and `ApiError` (including optional `code`) and update docs (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/PROJECT_LOG.md`, `docs/SCHEMA.md`, top-level `README.md`, and `apps/web/README.md`) to record the Prisma decision and current scaffolding. 

### Testing

- No automated tests were run because dependency installation and runtime (Prisma / Postgres) are blocked in this environment. 
- Basic repository validation steps (`git status`, file creation and commits) were executed successfully during the change.

author: scnerd
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a complete end-to-end testing suite using Playwright, enabling automated testing of the CarCalc application across user workflows including car management, cost calculations, settings, and maintenance data editing.

## Key Changes

### Testing Infrastructure
- **Added Playwright configuration** (`playwright.config.js`) with:
  - Chromium browser testing
  - Local dev server integration (trunk serve)
  - HTML reporting and trace collection
  - 2-minute timeout for WASM compilation
  - Base URL configuration for localhost:8080

- **Added package.json** with Playwright 1.56.1 and Tailwind CSS dependencies

- **Added task commands** in Taskfile.yml:
  - `task test:e2e` - Run all Playwright tests (builds first)
  - `task test:e2e:ui` - Interactive UI mode for debugging
  - `task install:playwright` - Install Playwright, wasm-bindgen-cli (0.2.108), and Chromium

### Test Suites
- **cars.spec.js** (291 lines) - Car CRUD operations:
  - Empty state display
  - Adding/deleting cars
  - Expanding/collapsing car details
  - Filling out car information
  - localStorage persistence across reloads
  - Multiple car management
  - Car ID integrity after deletions

- **calculations.spec.js** (372 lines) - Cost calculation verification:
  - Remaining miles and years calculations
  - Fuel cost based on MPG and gas price
  - Annual vs. total cost breakdowns
  - Insurance cost annualization
  - Opportunity cost calculations
  - Dynamic recalculation when settings change
  - All cost breakdown fields visibility
  - Edge cases (zero MPG handling)

- **maintenance.spec.js** (332 lines) - Maintenance data editor:
  - Section expand/collapse functionality
  - Vehicle selection dropdown
  - localStorage database initialization
  - State persistence during session
  - Accessibility of controls
  - Integration with other page features

### Documentation
- **Updated Claude.md** with:
  - New Testing section documenting task commands
  - Maintenance task documentation
  - Comprehensive Playwright setup guide including:
    - Version pinning rationale (1.56.1, wasm-bindgen-cli 0.2.108)
    - Test directory structure
    - Common test patterns (WASM initialization, navigation, forms, localStorage)
    - Dev server requirements

## Implementation Details

- **WASM Initialization Handling**: Tests include proper waits for WASM to initialize (`waitForLoadState('networkidle')` + 1000ms buffer)
- **localStorage Management**: Each test clears localStorage before running to ensure test isolation
- **Flexible Selectors**: Uses Playwright's role-based and label-based selectors for resilience
- **CI/CD Ready**: Configuration includes CI-specific settings (retries, single worker, forbidOnly)
- **Interactive Debugging**: UI mode support for test development and troubleshooting

## Testing Coverage
- 291 lines: Car management (CRUD, persistence, state)
- 372 lines: Cost calculations (formulas, updates, edge cases)
- 332 lines: Maintenance data editor (UI interactions, storage)
- **Total: 995 lines of test code** covering critical user workflows

## Summary
Introduces two new SQLAlchemy models to support AI-driven insight generation from aggregated marketing and revenue data. These models enable the system to store generated business insights and track their generation jobs with full tenant isolation and security controls.

## Key Changes

### New Models
- **AIInsight** (`src/models/ai_insight.py`): Stores AI-generated business insights with:
  - Classification by type (spend anomaly, ROAS change, etc.) and severity (info/warning/critical)
  - Template-based natural language summaries for determinism
  - Supporting metrics with period-over-period comparisons
  - Confidence scoring and content hashing for deduplication
  - Read/dismiss status tracking for UI interactions
  - Tenant isolation via `TenantScopedMixin`

- **InsightJob** (`src/models/insight_job.py`): Tracks insight generation job execution with:
  - Status lifecycle (queued → running → success/failed/skipped)
  - Cadence support (daily/hourly) based on tenant entitlements
  - Result tracking (insights generated, error messages)
  - Job metadata for contextual information
  - Tenant isolation via `TenantScopedMixin`

### Supporting Changes
- Updated `src/models/__init__.py` to export new models and enums
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `src/tests/unit/test_ai_insight_models.py` covering:
  - Enum validation
  - Model instantiation and properties
  - State transition methods
  - Helper properties (`is_unread`, `is_active`, `is_terminal`)

## Implementation Details

**Security**: Both models inherit from `TenantScopedMixin` ensuring tenant_id is only extracted from JWT tokens, never from client input. No raw data access—insights are generated from aggregated marts only.

**Determinism**: AIInsight uses content hashing (SHA256) for deduplication, ensuring identical insights for the same period are not duplicated.

**Database Optimization**: Strategic indexes on tenant_id, generated_at, insight_type, and status for efficient querying. Unique constraint prevents duplicate insights per tenant/period.

**State Management**: InsightJob includes helper methods (`mark_running()`, `mark_success()`, `mark_failed()`, `mark_skipped()`) for clean state transitions with automatic timestamp management.

author: aminghadersohi
body:
### SUMMARY

Fixes a regression from #37213 where MCP list tools (`list_datasets`, `list_charts`, `list_dashboards`) were not filtering response data when using default columns.

**Root Cause:**
PR #37213 fixed the `model_validate()` bug but accidentally changed the filtering logic to only apply when `select_columns` was explicitly provided:

```python
if request.select_columns:  # Only filters when explicitly provided
    return result.model_dump(mode="json", context={"select_columns": request.select_columns})
return result.model_dump(mode="json")  # No filtering for defaults!
```

This meant that when no `select_columns` was specified (using defaults), all 40+ columns were returned with `null` values, even though `columns_requested` showed only the minimal default columns.

**Fix:**
Always filter based on `columns_requested` (which contains either explicit `select_columns` or the defaults):

```python
columns_to_filter = result.columns_requested
return result.model_dump(mode="json", context={"select_columns": columns_to_filter})
```

### BEFORE/AFTER SCREENSHOTS OR ANIMATED GIF

**Request:** `{"page": 2}` (no select_columns)

**Before (broken):** Each dataset has all 40+ fields with null values
```json
{"datasets":[
  {"id":34,"table_name":"threads","schema_name":"public","database_name":null,"description":null,"changed_by":null,"changed_on":null,"changed_on_humanized":null,"created_by":null,"created_on":null,"columns":[],"metrics":[],...},
  ...
]}
```

**After (fixed):** Only the default columns are returned
```json
{"datasets":[
  {"id":34,"table_name":"threads","schema_name":"public","uuid":"d7438be6-..."},
  ...
]}
```

### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS

1. Start Superset with MCP service enabled
2. Call `list_datasets` with just `{"page": 1}` (no select_columns)
3. Verify response datasets only contain default columns: `id`, `table_name`, `schema_name`, `uuid`
4. Verify non-default columns like `description`, `database_name`, `changed_by`, etc. are NOT present (not even with null values)
5. Repeat for `list_charts` and `list_dashboards`

author: lingaom
body:
NVS writes an entry by first programming the data area and then writing the corresponding ATE. If a power loss occurs after the data has been written but while the ATE is being programmed, and the remaining space in the sector is only large enough for a single ATE, the ATE may end up partially written.

1) Power loss while writing the last data ATE, leaving only space for
   a delete ATE but no space for additional data entries:

       [ data ][ data ][ erase ][ ATE ][ ATE ][ erase ](sector end)
                                  ^^^
In this cases, nvs_startup() scans the sector and fails to find any erased space usable for data writes, causing mount to fail.

       [ data ][ data ][ erase ][ ATE ][ ATE ][ erase ]
               ^       ^           ^
                    ate_wra     Invalid
            data_wra

The sector is logically exhausted and should be closed and garbage collected.

Detect this condition during startup. If no erased space exists after the last ATE write, explicitly close the sector and trigger garbage collection to restore a writable sector.

This completes the missing recovery path for power-loss scenarios where a sector becomes effectively full due to ATE writes.

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/103029

# Description

<!-- Describe what this request will change/fix and provide any details necessary for reviewers. -->

This PR upgrades all Python dependencies to their latest versions (excluding linting tools like
`mypy` and `ruff`). Both `pyproject.toml` files (minimum version constraints) and `uv.lock` files
(locked versions) have been updated.

## redis-py Upgrade: 5.2.1 -> 6.4.0

This upgrade is noteworthy because it includes the fix for the deadlock issue reported in #1059.

Previously, CLP was locked to redis-py 5.2.1 via #1213 as a workaround for a deadlock bug in the
Redis PubSub implementation. The deadlock occurred when `AsyncResult.__del__()` issued a Redis
`UNSUBSCRIBE` while another frame held the PubSub lock.

With this upgrade to redis-py 6.4.0, the fix from redis/redis-py#3677 is now
included. Future redis-py upgrades (up to but not including 6.5.0 due to kombu's constraint) should
no longer cause the deadlock issue.

Note: redis-py 7.1.0 is the latest version on PyPI, but kombu (a dependency of celery) has a
constraint `redis<6.5`, so 6.4.0 is the maximum compatible version currently.

body:
Implements Item A1/A2 in src/backtest/engine.py (scope-limited to engine pipeline).\n\nKey semantics:\n- Two-pass flow: preview (first allocation_estimation_bars) -> weights -> full runs -> combine.\n- Single weighting point: portfolio_equity[t] = Σ w_i * equity_i[t] (no initial_cash scaling).\n- risk_parity v1: inverse-vol weights (std-floor epsilon).\n- sharpe_weighted v1: Sharpe -> clip(0,+inf) -> renorm; ValueError if all weights are 0.\n- Deterministic: strategy order sorted.\n- No silent equal-weight fallback for these methods.\n\nConfig knobs:\n- allocation_estimation_bars (default 500)\n- risk_free_rate (default 0.0)\n\nTests:\n- uv run pytest -q tests/backtest/test_engine_allocations.py\n- uv run ruff format --check src/backtest/engine.py tests/backtest/test_engine_allocations.py\n\nRisk/NO-LIVE: backtest-only engine + tests.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Introduces a deterministic two-pass allocation flow for portfolio backtests with robust error handling and numeric stability.
> 
> - `run_portfolio_from_config`: sorts `strategies`, adds two-pass preview for `risk_parity`/`sharpe_weighted`, defaults `allocation_estimation_bars` to 500, supports `risk_free_rate`, and applies a single weighting point (no pre-scaling of per-strategy `initial_cash`).
> - New helpers: `
>   - `_equity_to_returns_preview` (first-N bars preview returns)
>   - `_weights_inverse_vol` (inverse-vol, eps floor)
>   - `_weights_sharpe_long_only` (Sharpe, clip negatives, renorm)
>   - `_combine_equities_weighted` (Σ w_i * equity_i)
>   - `_calculate_allocation_from_preview_returns` (shared weighting logic with stability checks)`
> - Strengthened validation: deterministic ordering, index alignment, non-finite checks, epsilon floors, and explicit failure modes.
> - Tests: add `tests/backtest/test_engine_allocations.py` and extend two-pass tests to verify determinism, clipping/renorm, zero-vol regularization, insufficient data, and equality of allocations across runs.
>

body:
### Motivation
- Support a new inline file token syntax `@文本@(文件信息)` so previews can include clickable file links that open file previews. 
- Make stored app media easier to manage by grouping files by resource and type in the storage manager and enabling quick copy of file info to the clipboard.

### Description
- Add parsing of file tokens and a `FileSegment` to `PreviewTextBlock` with `parseFileSegments` so `@label@(info)` parts render as clickable labels and propagate clicks via a new `onFilePreview` callback. 
- Add `ResourceFileInfo` and helper functions `encodeResourceFileInfo` / `decodeResourceFileInfo` to encode/decode file metadata (`type` + `uri`) used for clipboard copy and preview handling. 
- Wire file preview handling into `ResourcePreviewScreen`, add `handleFilePreview` to decode the token payload and show a `FilePreviewDialog` that supports image, video (`MediaPreview`), and audio (`AudioPreviewSingle`). 
- Rework storage management in `ManageStorageScreen` (in `ResourceScreen`) to group stored files by type and resource title, present collapsible sections (`StorageSectionHeader`), and long-press copies encoded file info to the clipboard via `copyFileInfo`. 
- Propagate the new `onFilePreview` parameter where `PreviewTextBlock` is used (e.g. `CharacterScreen`) and make `MediaPreview` accept an optional `modifier` for reuse in dialogs.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: litmsctbb
body:
### Motivation
- The search UI was reporting "No MIDI found" despite scrapers discovering links because detail pages or HTML were being returned instead of raw .mid content and the client only showed a generic message. 
- Make scraping more robust across BitMidi, FreeMidi, MidiDB and MidiWorld by following detail/download pages, using realistic request headers, and verifying actual MIDI bytes before returning data to the client.

### Description
- Add `DEFAULT_HEADERS` and use them on all search/detail requests to reduce server-side blocking and improve HTML responses. 
- Widen link extraction in `extractMidiLinks` to include `.mid`/`.midi`, common download anchors and links whose text contains "midi", and preserve anchor text for smarter heuristics. 
- Introduce `isHtmlResponse` to detect HTML payloads and `fetchMidiFromUrl` which fetches a URL, validates MIDI signature (`MThd`), and falls back to parsing linked candidates from an HTML detail page (with one recursion depth). 
- Update each source handler (`fetchMidiFromBitMidi`, `fetchMidiFromFreeMidi`, `fetchMidiFromMidiDb`, `fetchMidiFromMidiWorld`) to try the top-ranked candidates (up to 5) and use `fetchMidiFromUrl` so detail pages are followed and only real MIDI buffers are returned. 
- Improve client search error handling in `client/src/App.jsx` to parse and surface backend JSON `error` payloads so the UI shows the real failure reason instead of a generic "No MIDI found" message.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for these changes.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds a new two-phase hybrid search path and updates Vespa schema/rank profiles for collapse sorting, which can affect query behavior and performance for collapsed searches. Risk is mitigated by schema version gating and extensive unit/integration test coverage.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new **`collapse.sortBy` feature** for hybrid search that can pick the representative document within each collapsed group based on a numeric field (e.g. lowest price), while keeping the overall group ordering from the relevance phase.
> 
> Implements a dedicated `CollapseSearch` flow that runs two hybrid searches (relevance collapse → sort-based collapse over collected group IDs) and merges hits, adding `_originalId` to track the replaced representative and handling `attributesToRetrieve` to avoid leaking internal fields.
> 
> Updates query/models to use a new `CollapseModel` (replacing the single `collapse_field_name`), adds schema/version gating (`2.24.13+`), extends Vespa query generation and schema templates with a `collapse_to_sort_value` rank profile and `marqo__collapse_sort_weights` query input, and adjusts filter handling to combine collapse sort filtering with existing filters. Extensive new unit + integration tests cover sorting, missing fields, disable rules vs main `sortBy`, facets parity, and merge semantics.

body:
Language switching fails on devices running Android 9-13 (API 28-33). The `overrideActivityTransition()` method used for smooth transitions is only available from API 34+.

## Changes

- Added API level check in `Activity.changeLanguage()` 
- Use `overridePendingTransition()` for API < 34
- Use `overrideActivityTransition()` for API ≥ 34

```kotlin
if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.UPSIDE_DOWN_CAKE) {
    overrideActivityTransition(Activity.OVERRIDE_TRANSITION_OPEN, ...)
} else {
    @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
    overridePendingTransition(...)
}
```

This restores functionality for ~70% of the user base while maintaining enhanced transitions on newer devices.

body:
## Summary

This PR fixes [RHOAIENG-41580](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHOAIENG-41580) by removing the duplicate "End Session" button from the session detail page.

## Problem

The session detail page had two buttons for ending sessions:
1. "Stop Session" button in the session header (REST API `/stop` endpoint)
2. "End Session" button in the MessagesTab component (WebSocket control message)

These buttons performed similar functions but with different implementations, causing user confusion about which one to use and what the difference was.

## Solution

Removed the duplicate "End session" button from the MessagesTab component, keeping only the "Stop Session" button in the session header as the canonical way to stop sessions.

### Changes Made

- Removed "End session" button from MessagesTab component (components/frontend/src/components/session/MessagesTab.tsx:701-709)
- Removed unused `ending` state variable
- Removed unused `handleEndSession` function
- Removed `onEndSession` prop from MessagesTabProps interface
- Updated Send button disabled condition to remove `ending` reference
- Removed `handleEndSession` handler from page.tsx
- Removed `onEndSession` prop from MessagesTab component usage

## Testing

- ✅ Frontend builds successfully (`npm run build`)
- ✅ Linter passes with no errors (`npm run lint`)
- ✅ TypeScript compilation succeeds
- ✅ "Stop Session" button in header remains functional

## Impact

- **User Experience**: Clearer, more consistent UX with a single button for stopping sessions
- **Code Quality**: Removed unused code and reduced complexity
- **Breaking Changes**: None - functionality remains the same, just consolidated

## Related Issues

Fixes: [RHOAIENG-41580](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHOAIENG-41580)

body:
## Doc Orchestrator Setup

This PR adds the GitHub Actions workflow required for automated documentation generation.

### What this workflow does

The Doc Orchestrator pipeline generates comprehensive documentation for your codebase:

1. **Inline Documentation** - Creates `.md` files next to source classes explaining their purpose
2. **CodeWiki Analysis** - Generates architecture overview and module documentation
3. **AI Tutorial Generator** - Claude-powered getting started guides and how-to tutorials

### Zero Configuration Required ✨

**No repository secrets needed!** All credentials (API keys, webhook secrets) are securely passed from the orchestrator at runtime via the dispatch payload. This means:

- ✅ No setup required - just merge this PR
- ✅ Credentials stay centralized and secure
- ✅ No manual secret management per repository

### How to trigger

Once merged, the workflow can be triggered in two ways:

1. **Via Multi-Platform-Hub**: Click "Run Pipeline" in the Doc Orchestrator dashboard
2. **Manual trigger**: Go to Actions → Doc Orchestrator Pipeline → Run workflow

### Files added

- `.github/workflows/doc-orchestrator.yml` - The GitHub Actions workflow

---

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces cross-SDK tool calling support, centralizing tool-call parsing and prompt building in the shared `runanywhere-commons` C++ implementation (default `…` and LiquidAI LFM2 formats), and wiring Swift/Kotlin/Flutter/React Native sample apps + SDK layers to use it. Key issues found: - Commons: tool-call `call_id` generation uses `time()*1000 + rand()%1000`, which can produce collisions/repeat deterministically if `rand()` isn’t seeded. - React Native SDK: `formatToolsForPrompt()` is now sync but returns raw JSON instead of a formatted prompt, which likely breaks existing callers. - Flutter SDK: follow-up prompts use default-format tool instructions even when the user selects a non-default format, which can cause inconsistent tool calling across iterations.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- This PR is mergeable but has a few correctness risks that can break tool-calling flows in specific SDKs. - Core changes are substantial but conceptually straightforward (centralize tool calling in commons). The main concerns are (1) non-robust call ID generation that can collide, (2) a React Native API behavior change where a sync formatter returns raw JSON, and (3) Flutter follow-up prompts using a mismatched tool-call format, which can cause inconsistent model behavior across iterations. - sdk/runanywhere-commons/src/features/llm/tool_calling.cpp, sdk/runanywhere-react-native/packages/core/src/Public/Extensions/RunAnywhere+ToolCalling.ts, sdk/runanywhere-flutter/packages/runanywhere/lib/public/runanywhere_tool_calling.dart

## Summary

- Adds `skillfish init` command that creates SKILL.md templates with YAML frontmatter for any detected AI agent
- Supports interactive mode (prompts for name, description, metadata, optional directories, location, agents) and non-interactive mode (CLI flags)

- YAML injection prevention via `yamlQuote()` with newline, backslash, and quote escaping
- Dual output: TTY with @clack/prompts and `--json` for automation
- Documents command structure conventions in CLAUDE.md for future consistency
- Adds init command reference and examples to README

author: rdhforeclosureconqueror-sys
body:
### Motivation
- Serve a static single-page frontend from the FastAPI app root so the UI and API can be deployed together without changing existing API routes.
- Ensure the repository runs the existing pytest suite automatically in the Docker environment at deploy/startup while not blocking a live service on test failures.

### Description
- Serve the frontend by mounting `frontend` at `/static` and returning `frontend/index.html` for `/` in `api/main.py` using `StaticFiles` and `FileResponse`, without changing API business logic.
- Add the frontend assets under `frontend/` (`index.html`, `app.js`, `styles.css`) and update the app to serve them from `/static` so resources load correctly in Docker.
- Add a `tests` service to `docker-compose.yml` that builds the same image and runs a non-blocking test runner script at container start.
- Add `scripts/run_tests_nonblocking.sh` which runs `pytest` inside the container, logs success or failure, and exits cleanly so failures do not stop the live service.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed during this change; the repo tests were not run as part of the PR update.
- The `tests` Docker service will execute the existing test suite with `pytest` inside the container when brought up, and it is implemented to log failures and exit without failing the deployment (`/app/scripts/run_tests_nonblocking.sh`).
- Test output and failure logs can be viewed from the deployment via `docker compose logs tests` or by inspecting the `tests` container logs in CI, and failures will be visible there without crashing the live service.

This PR introduces a “Mark all as read” action in the notifications interface, allowing users to mark all unread notifications as read with a single click.

Currently, users must mark notifications as read individually, which becomes repetitive and inefficient when multiple unread notifications are present. This change improves usability by reducing friction and aligning the notifications experience with common UX patterns.

- Adds a “Mark all as read” button to the notifications UI.
- Button is shown only when unread notifications exist.
- Marks all unread notifications as read in the backend.
- Updates the UI instantly (badge/count and read state).
- Preserves existing individual notification behavior.

Let's dive right in: - Free Up Space - Non-destructive editing - Database backup and restore (web) - Upload improvements - Visual refresh across all platforms - Disable admin setup - Star rating (mobile) - Additional fine-grained permissions (api keys) - Progressive JPEGs - Slideshow loop option (web) - Native HTTP clients for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 image loading ##### Free Up Space *This feature was requested ages ago. So long in fact, that it has a 3-digit ID ([#​165](https://redirect.github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/165))! Given the rapid iteration and development pace of the pre-stable era, it was risky to include it in the app due to its bulk-delete nature. But it is now 2026* :smile:*, so here we are.* **Free Up Space** allows you to remove local media files from your device that have already been successfully backed up to your Immich server (and are not in Immich trash). This helps reclaim storage on your mobile device without losing your memories. The feature can be accessed from the user profile panel or from the Settings page in the mobile app. There are configuration options and steps to make sure that everything is verified before deleting from the app. 1. **Configuration:** - **Cutoff date:** Free Up Space will only look for photos and videos **on or before** this date. - **Keep albums:** Hold all photos and videos in the selected albums on your device, regardless of other settings. By default, `**WhatsApp**` related albums are selected to be kept on the device. Assets that are not already on the device will not be redownloaded. - **Keep favorites:** This works the same way `**Keep albums**` . By default, favorited assets are preserved on your device. - **Keep on device:** You can choose to restrict removal to `**Always keep**` **All photos** or **All videos**, regardless of other settings. This setting can hamper freeing up space significantly — with 80 GB of videos and 40 GB of photos, selecting `**Always keep photos**` retains thousands of photos on your device. > \[!TIP] > These configurations are persistent to make it convenient for those who perform this task often. 2. **Scan & Review:** Before any files are removed, you are presented with a review screen to confirm which items will be deleted and how much storage will be reclaimed. 3. **Deletion:** Confirmed items are moved to your device's native Trash/Recycle Bin. > \[!NOTE] > **Reclaim storage** > To use the reclaimed space right away, you must manually empty the system/gallery trash outside Immich. For more information about this feature, please read it [here](https://docs.immich.app/features/mobile-app#free-up-space) ##### Non-destructive editing Immich now supports non-destructive photo editing. This means that any edits you make to an asset do not modify the original file; instead, the modifications are stored in the database, and new thumbnails are generated based on those changes. This means you can always revert to the original asset if needed. When you download an edited asset, Immich provides the edited version by default. However, you can choose to download the original version if needed. Immich always generates an edited full-size version based on your full-size quality settings. This occurs regardless of whether the "Enable full-size image generation" setting is enabled or disabled. > \[!NOTE] > **Limitations:** > > - Mobile clients must be updated to v2.5.0 in order view the edited version of an asset. Clients will continue to > see the original asset if on a mobile app version <2.5.0 > - As of this version, the edited download won't include the EXIF metadata of the original asset. This feature will come in future releases. > - Mobile editing still uses the old edit system (saving a new version of the photo). The mobile editor will be upgraded to use the new non-destructive editing system in a future release. You can click on the following icon to enter edit mode Currently, Immich supports the following types of edits: - Cropping - Rotation - Mirroring Opening the editor on an edited asset will load the existing edits back in so you can make adjustments and changes. ##### Backup and restore from the web UI Backup and restore are an important part of any self-hosted application; this feature helps you maintain reliable access to your instance during unexpected events, such as database corruption caused by system failure or power loss. Historically, restoring an Immich instance to a specific point required the user to have access to the command line, which proved challenging for many users, especially those new to self-hosting and software maintenance. Now, we have the entire backup and restore pipeline built into Immich, which allows you to quickly restore a database backup directly from the web UI. You can perform the steps either from the `Administration > Maintenance` page, or from a brand new instance on the welcome page. **Restore from Administration's Maintenance page** **Restore from Onboarding page** For more detailed steps, please read them in [our documentation](https://docs.immich.app/administration/backup-and-restore) ##### Upload improvement This release also improves foreground upload in the mobile app. The previous implementation improves background uploads but leaves foreground uploads less reliable by leveraging the queue system to offload upload handling to the OS, which can be throttled

author: tridge
body:
This adds an RC_OPTIONS bit which causes mode switch on resumption of R/C input after more than one minute of outage to be suppressed.
This is meant to safeguard against accidental mode switches in BVLOS flights where the pilot may not be careful enough with the transmitter while outside R/C range
Note that this only protects the mode switch, not AUX switches
