author: tumf
body:
## What
When using the Slack *extension* channel plugin (`extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`) the `read` action currently drops `threadId`, so `message read` cannot read thread replies via the extension path.

This PR forwards `threadId` from the extension plugin action handler to `handleSlackAction({ action: "readMessages", ... })` and adds a regression test.

## Why
Upstream already fixed the core adapter path in #1450 (passing `threadId` into `readSlackMessages`), but there are two code paths:

1) Core adapter path: `src/channels/plugins/slack.actions.ts` -> `src/agents/tools/slack-actions.ts` (fixed in #1450)
2) Extension plugin path: `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts` -> `runtime.channel.slack.handleSlackAction` (was still dropping `threadId` on `read`)

For users hitting the extension plugin path, thread reads are still broken without this change.

## Changes
- `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`: forward `threadId` for `action === "read"`
- `extensions/slack/src/channel.read-threadid.test.ts`: assert `threadId` is passed through

## Testing
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm test -- extensions/slack/src/channel.read-threadid.test.ts`

## References
- #1450 (core path fix): https://github.com/moltbot/moltbot/pull/1450

AI-assisted: OpenAI gpt-5.2 (reviewed locally).

author: dpacheconr
body:
## Summary

Add support for cascading registry, pullSecrets, and pullPolicy from global settings to nr-ebpf-agent.

### Phase 1: Global.Images.Registry Support ✅
- Updated values.yaml with clarifying comments for all 3 images
- Added kernelHeaderInstaller configuration (previously hardcoded)
- Added helpers to _helpers.tpl for all 3 images
- Updated both daemonset templates to use new image helpers

### Phase 2: Global.Images.PullSecrets Support ✅
- Updated both daemonsets (nr-ebpf-agent-daemonset.yaml, otel-collector-daemonset.yaml)
- Both use common library renderPullSecrets helper with concat
- Global and chart-level pullSecrets are concatenated together

### Phase 3: Global.Images.PullPolicy Support ✅ (NEW)
- Added pullPolicy helpers to _helpers.tpl for all 3 images
- Updated both daemonsets to use pullPolicy helpers
- Configuration respects hierarchy: global setting → chart-level setting → default (IfNotPresent)

## Configuration Hierarchy

**For Image Registry:**
1. `global.images.registry` (if set AND repository matches default)
2. Explicit repository configuration (takes precedence)

**For ImagePullSecrets:**
1. `global.images.pullSecrets` (highest priority)
2. Chart-level `pullSecrets`
Both sources are concatenated to support flexible secret management.

**For ImagePullPolicy:**
1. `global.images.pullPolicy` (highest priority)
2. Chart-level image `pullPolicy`
3. Default: `IfNotPresent`

## Implementation Details

**Images covered:**
- Kernel header installer init container
- eBPF agent main container
- OpenTelemetry collector container

- If global.images.registry is set AND repository matches default, uses global registry
- If repository is explicitly set to custom value, that takes precedence
- If global registry is not set, defaults to original docker.io paths
- kernel-header-installer is now configurable (was previously hardcoded)
- PullPolicy hierarchy ensures global settings cascade down when no explicit chart configuration is provided

## Test Plan

**Phase 1 (Registry):**
- ✓ Global registry is used when set: my.private.registry.com/newrelic/newrelic-ebpf-agent
- ✓ Defaults to docker.io when global registry not configured
- ✓ Explicit repository configuration overrides global
- ✓ All 3 images respect the same configuration hierarchy

**Phase 2 (PullSecrets):**
- ✓ No pullSecrets set → No imagePullSecrets section rendered
- ✓ Global pullSecrets only → Uses global across all daemonsets
- ✓ Both global + chart pullSecrets → Uses both (global items first)

**Phase 3 (PullPolicy):**
- ✓ Global pullPolicy is used when set and no chart-level policy exists
- ✓ Defaults to IfNotPresent when neither global nor chart policy is set
- ✓ Explicit chart-level pullPolicy overrides global setting

## Impact

Once merged, users can now configure nr-ebpf-agent with comprehensive global image settings:

\`\`\`yaml
global:
  images:
    registry: "my.private.registry.com"
    pullSecrets:
      - name: my-registry-credentials
    pullPolicy: Always
\`\`\`

**Note:** Rebased from upstream/master. Original PR #2004.

- Inline SVG for map pin icon replacing Lucide dependency.

author: rzvdev
body:
### Motivation

- Prevent stale highlights from persisting on the overlay when OCR/stabilization stops reporting a username by expiring highlights after a short TTL (measured in OCR frames). 
- Provide a configurable decay and an optional empty-highlight reset heuristic to avoid showing stale or spurious overlays during scrolling/noisy OCR. 

### Description

- Added two new scan options to `ScanSessionOptions`: `HighlightTtlFrames` and `HighlightEmptyResetFrames`, and wired defaults into the CLI and UI builders (`CliCommandHandlers`, `ScanningTabViewModel`).
- Updated `ScanSessionController.RunLoopAsync` to track an `ocrFrameIndex` and per-username `lastSeenFrames` dictionary, maintain an `emptyHighlightStreak`, and only update `lastSeenFrames` when the stabilizer returns fresh highlights.
- Implemented TTL expiry logic that removes usernames whose `lastSeen` age exceeds `HighlightTtlFrames`, clears tracking on scroll resets, and optionally clears highlights when `candidates.Count > 0` but no stabilized highlights are produced for `HighlightEmptyResetFrames` consecutive OCR frames.
- Updated test builders to include the new `ScanSessionOptions` parameters (`src/tests/.../ScanLifecycleTests.cs`, `ScanSessionControllerTests.cs`).

### Testing

- No automated test suite was executed in this change; unit test sources were updated to accommodate the new `ScanSessionOptions` parameters.
- Local compile/build was implied by editing and committing the changes, but `dotnet test` was not run as part of this PR.

body: # Pull Request ## 📋 Description Dungeon Crawler JS is a procedurally generated, rogue-lite RPG built with vanilla JavaScript and HTML5 Canvas. Unlike static grid games, this project implements: Drunkard’s Walk Algorithm: Generates organic, interconnected cavern systems for every new floor, ensuring 100% reachability for the exit stairs. *A Search Pathfinding:** Enemy AI utilizes a graph-based search with Manhattan distance heuristics to navigate around walls and hunt the player. Entity-Component System: A modular architecture for managing the player, diverse enemy types (Goblins/Orcs), and environmental triggers. Dynamic Viewport Engine: A responsive rendering system that keeps the player centered and scales to any window size without losing pixel-perfect clarity. author: immolo
body:
Enable experimental powerpc builds with dist kernel.

Catalyst builds can be tricky to replicate.
So this build will remove uncertainty and give clear roadmaps on what needs solving next.

The main test is will Catalyst build a ppc64be or ppc32 kernel by default and allow us to know which system will need a planned solution to let the other type build.

If ppc32 is built then we can test IBM and Apple boot support at the same time with the help of the PowerPC project.

PPC was picked first as it has a lot of interesting kernel hardware support quirks which match ALPHA and HPPA while have solid base to work from so we can
purely focus on Catalyst/Portage issues and not adding another layer of complexity surrounding gentoo-kernel and new arch hardware support.

### Motivation
- Improve the app UI to feel more like a compact “map explorer” dashboard while preserving all existing calculations and data-processing logic.

### Description
- Add a new top-level `Map view` tab implemented with `pydeck` that displays city points and a `ScatterplotLayer` with tooltips showing city, province, scenario(s), and season, and a small legend when coloring by province.
- Provide fallback coordinates via a small hardcoded `CITY_COORDS` dict for Islamabad, Karachi, Lahore, Peshawar, and Quetta and add `build_map_points` and `render_color_legend` helper functions plus a `PROVINCE_COLORS` palette.
- Reorganize sidebar controls into collapsible expanders (`Data source`, `Filters`, and `Map tools`) and add map-specific controls (`Reset map`, `Show city markers`, `Color by province`) while keeping the original filters and behavior intact.
- Inject light CSS styling (kept `st.set_page_config` as the first Streamlit call) to tighten padding, add subtle borders/rounded corners for metrics and expanders, and reduce max content width for a dashboard look; no analytical logic was modified.

### Testing
- Started the app with `streamlit run app.py` and executed an automated Playwright smoke test that opened the UI, switched to the `Map view` tab, and captured a screenshot successfully.
- Iteratively fixed pydeck argument issues found during the smoke test (removed unsupported `controller` and `height` kwargs); the final run completed without runtime errors and produced the expected map view screenshot.

Refactored timeout error handling constants to improve code organization and maintainability by consolidating error constants in a centralized location.

### Key Changes:

1. **Removed duplicate constants**: Deleted `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_ERROR_CODE` and `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_ERROR_MESSAGE` from `crates/pm_auth/src/consts.rs` and `crates/router/src/consts.rs`

2. **Centralized constants**: These constants are now imported from `hyperswitch_interfaces::consts` across the codebase

3. **Updated import statements**: Modified multiple files to import timeout constants from the centralized location:
   - `crates/router/src/core/payment_methods/access_token.rs`
   - `crates/router/src/core/payments/access_token.rs`
   - `crates/router/src/core/payouts/access_token.rs`
   - `crates/router/src/services/pm_auth.rs`

4. **Enhanced refund error handling**: Improved error handling logic in `crates/router/src/core/refunds.rs`:
   - Added conditional refund status update (only mark as `Failure` for non-5xx errors)
   - Prevented overwriting error codes/messages during timeout scenarios
   - Applied the same logic to both `trigger_refund_to_gateway` and `sync_refund_with_gateway` functions

This refactoring addresses code duplication and improves error handling consistency:

1. **Eliminates redundancy**: Having the same constants defined in multiple places (`router`, `pm_auth`) increases maintenance burden and risk of inconsistencies

author: shawaizn
body:
## Summary
Restructured the MainSidebar component to organize modules into three difficulty tiers (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced) with collapsible tier sections instead of individual module expansion.

## Key Changes
- **Tier-based organization**: Added `tiers` constant that groups modules by difficulty level with associated color schemes (blue for Beginner, amber for Intermediate, slate for Advanced)
- **Simplified state management**: Replaced `expandedModules` object with single `expandedTier` state to track which tier is currently expanded
- **Auto-expand functionality**: Added useEffect hook that automatically expands the tier containing the currently viewed module based on the URL pathname
- **Enhanced visual hierarchy**: 
  - Tier headers now display with color-coded backgrounds and left borders matching their difficulty level
  - Active tier/module states use tier-specific colors instead of uniform blue
  - Replaced ChevronUp/ChevronDown icons with ChevronRight/ChevronDown for better UX
- **Improved module display**: Added `shortenTitle()` utility function to truncate long module titles (max 30 characters) with ellipsis
- **Removed lesson-level navigation**: Simplified the sidebar by removing individual lesson links and recap links (now only shows module-level navigation)

## Implementation Details
- Color theming is centralized in the tier objects for easy maintenance and consistency
- The auto-expand logic uses regex to extract module ID from the current pathname and finds the corresponding tier
- Module links now display the module title instead of generic "Module N" labels
- Maintains responsive behavior with proper spacing and hover states for each tier level

author: ameykolhe
body:
## Summary

This PR merges several key improvements from development to main, focusing on website performance optimization, UI enhancements, and infrastructure refactoring:

- **Performance Optimizations**: Implemented comprehensive caching strategy with service worker for offline support, CDN cache headers, and resource hints (preconnect, dns-prefetch, preload)
- **UI Improvements**: Added customizable sidebar components with better structure and removed unused Svelte components
- **Infrastructure**: Refactored Airflow orchestration to use shared infrastructure Docker Compose setup

## Key Changes

### Website Performance (visualize/)
- Added service worker (`static/sw.js`) for offline caching with cache-first strategy for static assets and network-first for API data
- Configured Netlify CDN cache headers for immutable assets (1-year cache), API data (stale-while-revalidate), and static resources
- Added resource hints (preconnect, dns-prefetch) for critical CDNs (unpkg.com, CartoDB tiles)
- Implemented font preloading to prevent FOUT (Flash of Unstyled Text)
- Added Netlify build optimizations (CSS/JS bundling, minification, image compression)

**Expected Impact**: 30-40% faster initial loads, 80-90% faster repeat visits

### UI Enhancements
- Implemented customizable sidebar components with improved structure
- Cleaned up unused Svelte components from visualize directory

### Infrastructure
- Moved Airflow orchestration to shared infrastructure Docker Compose configuration
- Better separation of concerns and easier maintenance

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify cache headers after deployment: `curl -I https://[site-url]/_app/immutable/...`
- [ ] Check service worker registration in Chrome DevTools → Application → Service Workers
- [ ] Run Lighthouse audit to verify performance improvements (target: FCP <1.5s, LCP <2.5s, TTI <3s)
- [ ] Test offline functionality by going offline after initial load
- [ ] Verify sidebar components render correctly
- [ ] Confirm Airflow orchestration works with new Docker Compose setup

body:
## Context

Oh boy - it's a biggin!

This fixes most of the deprecation warnings when building CSS assets with SCSS. Most notably the use of `@import` which has now been updated to use `@use`.
SCSS no longer loads helpers/methods into the global space, therefore changes for [colour functions](https://github.com/DFE-Digital/apply-for-teacher-training/pull/11617/changes/e1161129c1260ff1be3627472db030b2fc87b91d) and [map-keys](https://github.com/DFE-Digital/apply-for-teacher-training/pull/11617/changes/95dc0aaae88ebc0bce1258b48da0b7cc83fe469f) are needed.

There are still some uses of `@import` due to the packages that they depend on - notable the MOJ frontend and DFE Autocomplete.

## Changes proposed in this pull request

This PR switches `@import` for `@use`, which also required the additional namespace changes when referencing variables/functions from other files - examples can be seen in this [commit](https://github.com/DFE-Digital/apply-for-teacher-training/pull/11617/changes/c90c1c50846164e380f23f11902868d292a4edc1)

There is also a [small change to the build script](https://github.com/DFE-Digital/apply-for-teacher-training/pull/11617/changes/a1afa3b7c40ca4f9071d09573af2af031c978789) to allow deprecation warnings to be silenced, when they originate from a dependancy. This is to cut down on unfixable noise.

## Guidance to review

Visually check assets in review app

View deprecation warnings when developing locally. Warnings will appear in relation to the MOJ and DFE Autocomplete partials.

`Warning: 14 on the type scale is deprecated and will be removed as a possible option in the next major version`
There is an outstanding deprecation warning for the use of a font size - this remains and should be addressed by developers & designers. 


## Things to check

- [ ] If the code removes any existing feature flags, a data migration has also been added to delete the entry from the database
- [ ] API release notes have been updated if necessary
- [ ] If it adds a significant user-facing change, is it documented in the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)?

- [ ] This code adds a column or table to the database
  - [ ] This code does not rely on migrations in the same Pull Request

  - [ ] data insights team has been informed of the change and have updated the pipeline
  - [ ] the sanitise.sql script and 0025-protecting-personal-data-in-production-dump.md ADR have been updated
  - [ ] does the code safely backfill existing records for consistency

author: twalmsley
body:
## Summary
Fixes issue #49 by displaying informative error messages when invalid order status transitions occur in the admin UI.

## Problem
When invalid order status transitions occur (e.g., PENDING → DISPATCHED), the system logs a clear message but the UI displays a generic error message "Failed to update order status: null" instead of the informative transition message.

## Root Cause
The `InvalidOrderStatusException` doesn't override `getMessage()`, so it returns `null`. When caught as a generic `Exception` in `AdminWebController.updateOrderStatus()`, the error message becomes "null".

## Solution
1. Added specific catch block for `InvalidOrderStatusException` in `AdminWebController.updateOrderStatus()` that formats a user-friendly error message showing the invalid transition (e.g., "Invalid status transition: PENDING → DISPATCHED").
2. Overrode `getMessage()` in `InvalidOrderStatusException` for consistency across all usages.

## Changes
- `AdminWebController.java`: Added import and specific catch block for `InvalidOrderStatusException`
- `InvalidOrderStatusException.java`: Overrode `getMessage()` method

## Testing
- All existing tests pass
- The fix ensures that invalid transitions now display: "Invalid status transition: {currentStatus} → {requiredStatus}" instead of "Failed to update order status: null"

Closes #49

Project stakeholder requested technical documentation covering current architecture and enhancement opportunities for the BIG-DAD platform (Laravel-based sugar dating application).

## Changes

- **New file**: `INFORME_PROYECTO.md` - Complete project analysis in Spanish including:
  - Stack inventory (Laravel 12, Mercado Pago integration, 17 models, 18 controllers)
  - Feature catalog (matching, messaging, moderation, payments, analytics)
  - Database schema overview (30 tables)
  - Test coverage summary (18 tests, 85%+ payment coverage)

## Improvement Roadmap

Documented 18 enhancement proposals prioritized across 3 tiers:

**High Priority** (P0):
- Identity verification automation (Stripe Identity/Onfido integration)
- Real-time notifications (Laravel Reverb WebSockets)
- Advanced search filters with ML recommendations
- AI-powered photo moderation (AWS Rekognition)
- PWA/native mobile app

**Medium Priority** (P1):
- Video calling (Twilio/Agora)
- Virtual gifts/token economy
- Referral program
- Events system
- Incognito mode

**Low Priority** (P2):
- OAuth social login
- Reputation/review system
- Multi-language support
- Gamification badges

Each proposal includes problem statement, implementation approach, and business impact.

## Additional Sections

- Security enhancements (2FA, E2E encryption, ML-based fraud detection)
- Performance optimizations (Redis migration, CDN, Elasticsearch)
- UX/UI improvements (onboarding, dark mode, microinteractions)

author: copilot
body:
The `@Command` decorator throws when applied to classes with no `@Field()`-decorated properties, forcing users to add placeholder fields to satisfy the metadata system.

## Root Cause

`getClassMetadata()` checks if `buildClassMetadataFromFields()` returns any fields/methods. When both are empty, it falls through to the old transformer-based system and throws an error.

## Changes

**`packages/core/src/decorators/metadata.ts`**
- Remove conditional that requires fields or methods to be present
- Always return metadata from new system, even when empty
- Fallback to old system only on actual errors

**`packages/core/test/decorators/command.test.ts`**
- Add test case for fieldless commands

## Example

```typescript
// Now works without placeholder fields
@Command({ authorize: 'all' })
export class CreateNote {
  public static async handle(_command: CreateNote, register: Register): Promise<UUID> {
    const noteId = UUID.generate()
    register.events(new NoteCreated(noteId))
    return noteId
  }
}
```

I'm not sure if this is compiler dependent or if it was just a poor fix, but some (all?) non RedHat systems complain about the use of `RHEL_RELEASE_VERSION`. The previous `!defined RHEL_RELEASE_CODE` should naively short circuit the check but it doesn't.

So this now explicitly checks if the system is RedHat before using `RHEL_RELEASE_VERSION`. I couldn't find a cleaner way of doing it, and I don't think a "one liner" is possible.

Description of issues

https://crowncommercialservice.atlassian.net/browse/AI-168
When the name match step is invoked after an MI entry doesn't merge with a contract entry, all of the names in the contracts file are used as potential options for matching. 

Impact

However, this means that if two suppliers use the same incorrect name for a buyer, the LLM will have the option to match on the incorrect name, which would mean that this MI entry doesn’t get matched.

Solution: remove the input name from the options, either at the stage of calling the function, or within the function

author: joshuaoliver
body:
## Summary
This PR enhances the analytics and reporting capabilities across the application by adding detailed drill-down views, real-time email tracking, and improved time tracking statistics.

## Key Changes

### Gmail Actions
- **New `getTodaySentCount` action**: Real-time public action to fetch today's sent email count from Gmail using Sydney timezone, enabling live updates on the dashboard

### Hubstaff Analytics
- **`getProjects` query**: Retrieve all unique projects with aggregated time tracking data, sorted by total hours
- **`getDailySummariesByProject` query**: Filter daily summaries by date range and optional project ID for granular analysis
- **`getDetailedDayData` query**: Drill-down view showing hourly breakdown by project with task-level details for a specific day
- **`getWorkingHoursStats` query**: Comprehensive working hours statistics including average hours per business day, per week, and weekday breakdown

### RescueTime Analytics
- **`getDetailedDayComparison` query**: Hourly comparison between RescueTime and Hubstaff data, identifying potentially missed billable hours with category breakdowns

### UI Enhancements

**Hubstaff Page (`hubstaff.tsx`)**
- Added working hours statistics card with business day averages and weekday breakdown
- Implemented date range selector (7, 14, 30, 60, 90 days)
- Added project filter dropdown for filtering daily summaries
- Interactive daily chart with click-to-drill functionality
- New modal dialog for detailed day breakdown showing:
  - Project time distribution with percentages
  - Task-level time entries with activity percentages
  - Visual timeline representation of time allocation

**RescueTime Page (`rescuetime.tsx`)**
- Extended date range options to include 60 and 90 days
- Added interactive day selection in missed time report
- New modal dialog for hourly breakdown comparison showing:
  - Side-by-side RescueTime vs Hubstaff comparison
  - Hour-by-hour activity timeline with productive/other work distinction
  - Hubstaff project breakdown
  - Top RescueTime categories with percentages
  - Highlighted potentially missed hours with category information

**Today Page (`today.tsx`)**
- Integrated real-time email sent count using new `getTodaySentCount` action
- Falls back to snapshot-based count if real-time fetch is unavailable
- Added loading indicator during real-time fetch

**RescueTime Settings (`rescuetime.tsx`)**
- Added backfill options for 60 and 90 days (previously only 30 days available)

## Implementation Details
- All new queries use proper indexing (`by_date`) for efficient filtering
- Time calculations consistently use seconds internally with conversion to hours for display
- Date handling respects Sydney timezone for consistency across the application
- Modal dialogs provide rich drill-down experiences without navigation
- Visual representations use color-coded bars and timelines for quick pattern recognition
- Graceful fallbacks for missing data with appropriate empty states

author: nidhipednekar
body:
## What?
<!-- Link this PR to its associated issue with an appropriate keyword: Closes, See, Follow up to, etc. -->
Closes #74975

This PR fixes a visual gap next to the admin menu navigation triangle when pages are built using wp-build.

Specifically, it ensures the white navigation triangle overlaps the content border correctly, preventing a visible 1px gap.

## Why?
When pages in WP Admin (for example Appearance → Fonts) are built with the new wp-build package, a small border appears next to the navigation triangle.

This causes a noticeable visual inconsistency where the triangle does not blend seamlessly with the page content, making the UI look misaligned.

## How?
The fix adjusts the CSS for the admin menu navigation triangle so that it properly overlaps the content border.

This approach is based on the CSS behavior discussed in the issue and refined to align with existing admin menu styles, avoiding layout or sizing regressions.

## Testing Instructions

1. Open the WordPress admin dashboard.
2. Navigate to Appearance → Fonts.
3. Observe the admin menu navigation triangle.
4. Verify that the triangle blends seamlessly with the page content and that no visible border or gap appears.

Note: I was unable to run wp-env locally due to a known wp-env network issue on Windows. 
The fix was validated via isolated CSS testing and by following the issue reproduction steps.

### Testing Instructions for Keyboard

1. Open the WordPress admin dashboard.
2. Use the keyboard to navigate to Appearance → Fonts.
3. Ensure focus navigation works as expected.
4. Confirm that the navigation triangle remains visually aligned with the content and no layout shift or gap is visible.

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> This rewrites core cryptographic primitives (ECDSA/ECDH/ECIES) and changes key/ciphertext types from `Buffer` to `Uint8Array`, which can affect interoperability and security-sensitive behavior (e.g., key validation, signature formatting, padding/MAC handling). Extensive tests were added, but any subtle mismatch could break consumers.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Replaces the underlying crypto implementation** by swapping `elliptic` for `@noble/curves` across `sign`/`verify`, `derive`/`derivePadded`, and ECIES `encrypt`/`decrypt`, including new public/private key validation via noble utilities.
> 
> **Switches all binary inputs/outputs from `Buffer` to `Uint8Array`** (including the `Ecies` shape), updates hash/HMAC/AES plumbing to avoid `Buffer` helpers, and adjusts ECDH output behavior to preserve legacy “unpadded” semantics while keeping `derivePadded()` fixed at 32 bytes.
> 
> **Updates dependencies and tests**: removes `elliptic` from runtime deps, adds `@noble/curves`, introduces a dev-only `eccrypto-old` alias plus a comprehensive `backward_compatibility.spec.ts`, and tweaks browser test config to skip those node-only compatibility tests (removing the prior Buffer setup).

author: illianemploy
body:
Implemented minimal Godmode feature for testing enemy AI without player death:

Implementation (doctrine-compliant, allocation-free):

1. DebugConfig (GameEngine.kt):
   - Added godmode: Boolean field (primitive only)
   - Zero runtime cost when disabled

2. Damage Protection (GameEngine.kt applyDamageToPlayer):
   - Clamps playerHealth to minimum 1 when godmode enabled
   - Single if-check after damage application
   - Prevents isAlive = false while godmode active
   - Debug-gated: BuildConfig.DEBUG && debugConfig.godmode

3. Input Event (InputEvent.kt):
   - Added ToggleGodmode to DebugStress sealed class
   - Reuses existing debug input infrastructure

4. Event Handler (GameEngine.kt handleDebugStress):
   - Added ToggleGodmode case to existing when block
   - Toggles godmode flag via copy() (UI input, not hot path)

5. UI Toggle (MainActivity.kt):
   - Added Switch control in debug stress test section
   - Red colors indicate critical debug feature
   - Calls handleDebugStress(ToggleGodmode) on change

6. UI Indicator (MainActivity.kt):
   - Added "⚠️ GODMODE: ON" warning at top-center
   - Red bold text, visible when godmode active
   - Only renders when BuildConfig.DEBUG && godmode enabled

Technical details:
- Zero per-frame allocations (single boolean check)
- No new systems, abstractions, or iterators
- Minimal diffs: 4 lines GameEngine, 1 line InputEvent, ~20 lines UI
- Debug-only: gated by BuildConfig.DEBUG where exposed
- Single source of truth: DebugConfig.godmode

Behavioral guarantees:
- Godmode ON: Player cannot die (health clamps to 1)
- Godmode OFF: Identical to current behavior
- Damage feedback preserved (numbers, i-frames, shield)
- Adaptive difficulty tracking unaffected

Use case: Test enemy AI behaviors (dodge, burst, formations) without
         constant death interruption during development.

No performance impact, doctrine-compliant, minimal surface area.

@
This pull request updates documentation to reflect that Triton Inference Server is now the primary, production-ready backend for model serving in the DSA Agent project, replacing the previous FastAPI-based approach. The changes streamline setup instructions, clarify architecture, update endpoint details, and emphasize GPU-accelerated, dynamically batched inference. The documentation now focuses on Triton’s usage, configuration, and monitoring, and removes outdated references to the FastAPI server as the main inference entrypoint.

**Key Documentation Updates:**

**1. Triton-Centric Architecture & Setup**
- All architecture diagrams, directory structures, and quick start instructions now focus on Triton as the main inference server, with FastAPI references removed or minimized. The Triton model repository path is updated to `agent/serving/triton/models/`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7025a5b5dd9966c29748c2d6e5da77d68510362e621a3a08e0ed82e965f787bbL5-R57) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-aea606d6d4b2eb40933760bfd01402b57e5784634fb044ff5e125c6d5dc3bed5L5-R11) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-aea606d6d4b2eb40933760bfd01402b57e5784634fb044ff5e125c6d5dc3bed5L22-R28) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-aea606d6d4b2eb40933760bfd01402b57e5784634fb044ff5e125c6d5dc3bed5L46-R85)
- Docker orchestration and startup instructions are simplified to use `docker-compose up --build` for Triton, eliminating the previous shell script and FastAPI-specific steps. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7025a5b5dd9966c29748c2d6e5da77d68510362e621a3a08e0ed82e965f787bbL69-R109) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-aea606d6d4b2eb40933760bfd01402b57e5784634fb044ff5e125c6d5dc3bed5L46-R85)

**2. Endpoint and Port Standardization**
- All API endpoint references, health checks, and client examples are updated to use Triton’s ports: HTTP/REST on 8000, gRPC on 8001, and metrics on 8002. FastAPI endpoints and ports are removed from guides and tables. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7025a5b5dd9966c29748c2d6e5da77d68510362e621a3a08e0ed82e965f787bbL69-R109) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7025a5b5dd9966c29748c2d6e5da77d68510362e621a3a08e0ed82e965f787bbL159-R130) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7025a5b5dd9966c29748c2d6e5da77d68510362e621a3a08e0ed82e965f787bbL193-R167) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7025a5b5dd9966c29748c2d6e5da77d68510362e621a3a08e0ed82e965f787bbL209-R182) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-7025a5b5dd9966c29748c2d6e5da77d68510362e621a3a08e0ed82e965f787bbL232-R213) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-7025a5b5dd9966c29748c2d6e5da77d68510362e621a3a08e0ed82e965f787bbL290-R260) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-aea606d6d4b2eb40933760bfd01402b57e5784634fb044ff5e125c6d5dc3bed5L46-R85)

**3. Feature and Performance Documentation**
- The performance comparison now highlights Triton’s dynamic batching, gRPC support, and production readiness. FastAPI is no longer compared as a peer inference backend.
- Batch inference, gRPC usage, and performance monitoring sections are updated to use Triton’s endpoints and Python client. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7025a5b5dd9966c29748c2d6e5da77d68510362e621a3a08e0ed82e965f787bbL209-R182) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7025a5b5dd9966c29748c2d6e5da77d68510362e621a3a08e0ed82e965f787bbL232-R213)

**4. Removal of Deprecated Content**
- The README and guides remove sections about FastAPI endpoints, file structure, and project evolution, focusing instead on Triton and the current agentic architecture. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L447-R447) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L619-L699)

**5. Next Steps and References**
- Next steps now include testing with the VS Code extension, implementing RAG features, and monitoring via Prometheus/Grafana, with references to new documentation and performance guides.

These updates ensure the documentation accurately reflects the project’s current architecture and best practices for high-performance, production-ready model serving with Triton.

body:
- [x] **Disable M and F extensions** - Set `ENABLE_M_EXT=0` and `ENABLE_F_EXT=0` in fpga_top.sv
- [x] **Add address mapping logic** - Create proper address translation from CPU addresses (0x80000000+) to block RAM offsets (0+)
  - Instruction memory: Maps 0x80000000+ to BRAM byte offset 0+
  - Data memory: Maps 0x80000000+ to BRAM byte offset 0+
- [x] **Add address range validation** - Properly check if addresses are within valid DRAM range
  - Added `imem_addr_valid` and `dmem_addr_valid` signals to check address bounds
  - Gated BRAM control signals (`imem_req_gated`, `dmem_req_gated`, `dmem_we_gated`, `dmem_re_gated`)
  - Returns 0 for reads from invalid addresses, drops writes to invalid addresses
  - Asserts ready immediately for invalid addresses (no BRAM access needed)
- [x] **Fix byte addressing** - Pass full non-aligned byte addresses to BRAMs for compressed instruction and sub-word access support
  - Updated bram_imem.sv and bram_dmem.sv to accept 12-bit byte addresses
  - BRAM modules now internally calculate word address and byte offset
- [x] **Fix OR instruction encoding** - Changed `mem[10]` from `32'h00F76593` (I-type) to `32'h00F765B3` (R-type OR)
- [x] **Fix stub_div.sv width** - Changed `32'h0` to `'0` for width-generic zero
- [x] **Use global clock network** - Changed PLL to use `PLLOUTGLOBAL` instead of `PLLOUTCORE` for reduced skew
- [x] **Update test program** - Match LED pattern behavior from led_demo/led_pattern_top.sv:
  - Initial pattern: 0xAA (10101010)
  - Rotate left by 1 bit every second
  - Alternates between 0xAA and 0x55
- [x] **Add PLL for timing closure** - Generate 25 MHz system clock from 100 MHz input
  - Uses iCE40 `SB_PLL40_CORE` primitive with global clock output
  - Design achieves 32.73 MHz max (PASS at 25 MHz target)
- [x] **Add stub modules** - Created stub_fpu.sv and stub_div.sv for Yosys module resolution

body:
### Motivation

- Notices were being labeled as "past" based only on the date, which caused same-day events with later times to appear as past prematurely.
- The goal is to classify a notice as past only after its scheduled end time in Nepal time.

### Description

- Added `NEPAL_TIMEZONE_OFFSET`, `parseTimeSlotEnd`, and `getNoticeEndDate` helpers to parse a notice `timeSlot` (AM/PM with optional minutes) and derive an end `Date` using a safe end-of-day fallback.
- Replaced date-only comparisons with end-time comparisons against the current time (`now`) so notices become past only after the scheduled end time.
- Updated the `useMemo` filtering and the compact/detailed rendering logic to use the new end-time calculation and removed the unused `getLocalToday` import.
- Modified `frontend/src/pages/NoticesPage.tsx` to implement the above changes.

### Testing

- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: panoskou
body:
## Summary
This PR removes unused dependencies, consolidates duplicate protobuf library versions, and refactors rate limiting and TCP/UDP proxy initialization to be more maintainable and correct.

## Key Changes

### Dependency Management
- Removed unused `cmake` crate dependency from `prost-build`
- Removed duplicate `tonic-build` 0.7.2 dependency (kept only 0.9.2)
- Consolidated `prost`, `prost-types`, and `prost-build` to single versions (0.11.9)
- Removed `tonic-build = "0.7"` from Cargo.toml

### Rate Limiting Refactor
- Renamed `rate_per_sec` and `rate_burst` variables to `rate_limit` and `rate_period` for clarity
- Changed rate limiting to use `Duration::from_secs(1)` instead of configurable burst duration
- Updated both HTTP and HTTPS gateway calls to pass rate limit as `u64` and period as `Duration`
- Added clarifying comments about RateLimitLayer behavior

### TCP/UDP Proxy Initialization
- Changed TCP proxy from single instance to per-backend spawning (iterates over backends with `protocol == "tcp"`)
- Changed UDP proxy from single instance to per-backend spawning (iterates over backends with `protocol == "udp"`)
- Removed bearer token authentication from TCP/UDP proxies (now uses service name instead)
- Updated logging to include service name for each spawned proxy instance
- Moved `http_port` variable capture to avoid closure issues

### Code Quality
- Fixed incorrect `#[warn(dead_code)]` attributes to proper `#[allow(dead_code)]` in:
  - `backend_registry.rs` (3 occurrences)
  - `config.rs` (4 occurrences)
- Removed obsolete comments about TLS configuration in config struct

## Implementation Details
The TCP/UDP proxy changes enable multiple backends of the same protocol type to be served simultaneously, with each backend getting its own gateway instance listening on the configured port. This is a more flexible approach than the previous single-instance design.

## About PR 📝

Add a **review-typescript-pull-request** skill so agents can perform structured, context-aware PR reviews for TypeScript, Node.js, and React. The skill defines when to use it (e.g. “review this PR”, “PR feedback”), a “before commenting” checklist (read PR description, examine modified files, understand scope), data gathering (use only `get_pull_request` and `get_pull_request_files`), a review workflow, and a required output format (Summary, TypeScript type safety, Testing coverage, Flow and integration analysis, Code quality and architecture, Strengths, Issues, Recommendations). The 3D skin preview only textured head and body, leaving arms and legs as solid colors. Additionally, the renderer only supported Slim models (3px arms) without a way to switch to Classic (4px arms).

## Changes

**Extended texture mapping to all body parts**
- Applied UV coordinates to arms and legs (previously solid color #99cc66)
- All parts now use standard Minecraft 64x64 skin format

**Added model type support**
- `Skin3DRenderer` constructor accepts `isSlim` parameter
- Dynamic UV mapping for Slim (3px) vs Classic (4px) arms
- `setModelType()` method enables runtime switching
- Arm width and positioning adjust automatically (offset 5.5 vs 6)

**UI controls**
- Model selector dropdown per skin entry
- Updates geometry metadata (`geometry.humanoid.customSlim` or `.custom`)
- Real-time 3D preview updates on selection change
- Persists to localStorage and skinpack manifest

```javascript
// Before: Only head and body were textured
const texturedParts = ['head', 'body'];

// After: All parts receive proper UV mapping
const allParts = ['head', 'body', 'rightArm', 'leftArm', 'rightLeg', 'leftLeg'];
allParts.forEach(partName => {
  // Apply texture with model-specific UV coordinates
  this.applyUVMapping(part, partName);
});
```

author: raphyduck
body:
### Motivation
- Provide partial, real-time job output via the API while a job is running so `/jobs/:id` returns incremental output instead of only after completion.
- Ensure speakers publish lines to the daemon job buffer as they are emitted so remote clients (CLI) can display progress immediately.
- Make the CLI follow and print only newly appended output during polling with immediate flushing.

### Description
- Initialized `Job#output` when a job is created with `capture_output: true` by setting `output` in `enqueue` (in `app/daemon.rb`).
- Reused `job.output` when starting execution and assigned `thread[:captured_output]` to the shared buffer so captured output is preserved and mutated during execution (`execute_job` changes in `app/daemon.rb`).
- Added `Daemon.append_job_output(jid, line, thread: ...)` to append lines to `job.output` incrementally without overwriting existing content (implemented in `app/daemon.rb`).
- Updated `SimpleSpeaker::Speaker#daemon_send` (in `lib/simple_speaker.rb`) to call `Daemon.append_job_output` when available and to avoid double-appending into thread capture buffers.
- Modified `Client#wait_for_job_completion` (in `app/client.rb`) to track an `output_cursor` and write only the new portion of `job['output']` to `$stdout` with immediate `flush`, returning when the job reaches a finished status.

### Testing
- Ran the automated test suite with `bundle exec rake test`, which failed to run because a bundler/git dependency was not installed (`archive-zip` repository requires `bundle install`), so tests could not be executed to completion.
- No other automated tests were added; behavior was verified by static inspection of the modified flow that initializes and appends `job.output` and that the client prints incremental output.

body:
## Summary

Our custom Sentry event filter was not working correctly because it assumed all events would have an exception in the `original_exception` field. When Sentry sent non-exception events (like messages or breadcrumbs), the filter would crash or behave unexpectedly.

This PR fixes the filtering by:
- Adding a guard clause (`when is_exception(exception)`) to only process actual exception events
- Integrating `Sentry.DefaultEventFilter.exclude_exception?/2` to respect Sentry's built-in filtering rules alongside our custom ignored exceptions list
- Updating Sentry dependency to the latest version

## Testing

Manual verification of the filter logic. This is a configuration-level change that ensures events flow through properly.

author: benruseau
body:
Return null on DevicePinger.ping() error to avoid unhandled promise rejection in RxJS subscription

<!--
Thank you for your contribution! 👍
Please make sure to read CONTRIBUTING.md if you have not already. Pull Requests that do not comply with the rules will be arbitrarily closed.
-->

### 📝 Description

When a device is connected to LW and then physically disconnected, the `DevicePinger` continues to send the `GetAppAndVersionCommand` command, which puts the state machine into the `WaitingForReconnectionWithQueuedSendApdu` state.

The issue occurs on `ReconnectionTimedOut`: an error APDU response (`DeviceDisconnectedBeforeSendingApdu`) is sent just before the connection is closed by the `ApduSender`. This error is logged by the `DevicePinger` (e.g. “Error while pinging device”), and then **rethrown**.

Rethrowing this error causes unhandled promise rejections in the `DevicePinger` RxJS subscription to `SessionEventDispatcher`, which is started by `DeviceSessionRefresher` when setting up a new device session. This can cause the DMK instance to crash.

To fix this, I replaced the error throw with a null return to comply with the `DevicePinger.ping` method signature and prevent the unhandled rejection.

author: twalmsley
body:
This PR implements comprehensive caching for service methods as outlined in issue #21.

## Changes

### Cache Configuration
- Added cache configurations for: flashSales, orders, orders:user, orders:all, users, and analytics caches
- Set appropriate TTLs: 1 minute for volatile data (flash sales, orders), 5 minutes for less volatile data (users, analytics)

### ProductsService
- Added @Cacheable to getAllProducts() and getProductStockById()
- Added @CacheEvict to createProduct() (evicts all products cache)

### FlashSalesService
- Added @Cacheable to getAllFlashSales() and getFlashSaleById()
- Added @CacheEvict to all update/create/delete methods with appropriate cache invalidation

### OrderService
- Added @Cacheable to getOrderById(), getOrderByIdForAdmin(), getOrdersByUser(), and getAllOrders()
- Added @CacheEvict to all update/create methods

### UserService
- Added @Cacheable to findById() and findByUsername()

### AnalyticsService
- Added @Cacheable to all read methods: getSalesMetrics(), getRevenueMetrics(), getProductPerformance(), getOrderStatistics()

## Testing
- All existing tests pass
- No regressions introduced

Fixes #21

author: takeyaqa
body:
This pull request refactors the `PictMCPServer` class to directly extend `McpServer` instead of wrapping it, and updates related code and naming for consistency. It also removes the now-unnecessary delegation unit tests.

Class refactoring and code simplification:

* Refactored `PictMCPServer` to extend `McpServer` directly, renaming it to `PictMcpServer` for consistency, and updated its construction and tool registration logic to use superclass methods. (`src/server.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8a8ae07582c9d433ec8c2e5c4310ff8901e604f4965c5b90a49117ad46c47595L2-R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8a8ae07582c9d433ec8c2e5c4310ff8901e604f4965c5b90a49117ad46c47595R27-R29)
* Removed redundant delegation methods (`connect`, `close`, `isConnected`, etc.) from the server class since they are now inherited from `McpServer`. (`src/server.ts`)

Naming consistency:

* Updated all references from `PictMCPServer` to `PictMcpServer` in the codebase, including the main entry point. (`src/index.ts`)

Testing cleanup:

* Removed the delegation unit tests for `PictMCPServer` as they are no longer applicable after the refactor. (`src/server.spec.ts`)

These changes simplify the codebase by leveraging inheritance, reduce boilerplate, and ensure naming consistency throughout the project.

author: j00bar
body:
Presently, dynamic actions via the `get_change_actions` and `get_changelist_actions` methods only impact the UI presentation of available actions. The class variables for `change_actions` and `changelist_actions` must contain all possible actions, and the BaseActionView will respond to action requests regardless of whether the tool is in change_actions or changelist_actions and regardless of whether `get_change_actions` or `get_changelist_actions` would include that action for the given request.

This PR fulfills the wishlist item to make the BaseActionView respond only to the actions permitted by the dynamic action functions and only for the type of action allowed.

It attempts to maintain as much backward compatibility as possible in doing so, with an eye toward minimizing any breakage for older, customized installations.

author: copilot
body:
Log exports were empty because logging only triggered under limited conditions (sun > 80°, specific load events). Need comprehensive data to diagnose sun brightness anomalies and sleep mode state corruption.

## Changes

**Sun/Brightness Logging** (`day_night_cycle.gd`)
- Log every 10s during day progression (was: only when sun > 80°)
- Added `_log_environment_state()` to capture full state: sun position, light energy, ambient brightness, environment settings, animation states
- Log at game start, sunrise/sunset transitions, night entry
- Added separate `last_sun_log_time` throttle variable (fixed bug: was sharing throttle with DebugLogOverlay causing per-frame logging)

**Sleep/Lifecycle Logging** (`day_night_cycle.gd`)
- Added `_notification()` handler for app pause/resume events
- Log all state transitions: day start, lockout expired, entering sleep
- Capture unix timestamps, lockout states, day count at each transition

**Player State Logging** (`player.gd`)
- Log position, rotation, camera mode, health, air on save load

## Result

Logs now populate from game start with periodic samples throughout gameplay. ZIP exports contain:
- Sun/brightness: sampled every 10s + all transitions
- Sleep state: all lifecycle events + app background/foreground
- Player state: load/restore events

Previous conditions would miss critical states (e.g., dark game at noon, corrupt state on resume). New logging captures complete diagnostic timeline.

this PR is another step for closing the distributed zstar conservation issue 

Edit: a couple of bugs including the `MutableVerticalDiscretization` and `SplitExplicitFreeSurface` were found
- The `surface_buffer_kernel_parameters` needs to include corners to make sure the column height is correctly computed when iterating the split explicit free surface
- In case of a non-distributed grid, we need to have topology-aware column_height operators that do not go and look in the halos when iterating the split explicit solution (this is `SplitExplicitFreeSurface` specific)
- topology-aware operators need to include the new topologies `RightCenterFolded` and `RightFaceFolded` which act the same as a `RightConnected` topology.

Closes #5161

author: kordan
body:
The editing teacher can add elements from his/her surveypro to a search form to search among the responses obtained for those that satisfy his/her search. If there is more than one element, such as “first name” and “last name,” and the user searches using only the “last name” element, which records should be found? Those with the “last name” element matching the one requested by the user, or those with (the “last name” element matching the one requested by the user) && (the “first name” element empty)?

To answer this question, each element of the form has a checkbox that disables it. If the box is selected, the corresponding element is disabled and vice versa.

So if the user writes a "last name" and leave the “ignore” box next to the "name" selected, he/she will only find responses with (the “last name” field equal to the requested one). If, on the other hand, the “ignore” box next to the name is deselected, then only responses with (the “last name” field equal to the requested one) && (the “first name” field empty) will be found.

When the search form consists of only one element, the "ignore" checkbox is useless! This update removes the checkbox in this particular case.

author: pritamchaurasiya
body:
🛡️ Sentinel: [CRITICAL] Fix race condition in coupon application

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: A race condition in `CouponService.apply_coupon` allowed users to redeem coupons beyond their usage limits by sending concurrent requests. The usage count was read into memory, incremented, and saved, creating a window where multiple requests could read the same initial value.
🎯 Impact: Financial loss due to unlimited coupon redemptions.
🔧 Fix: Implemented atomic updates using Django's `F()` expressions and added a conditional `update()` query (`used_count__lt=F('max_uses')`) to ensure limits are strictly enforced at the database level.
✅ Verification: Added a new test `store/tests/test_coupon_concurrency.py` which simulates concurrent requests and verifies that `used_count` never exceeds `max_uses`.

Also fixed configuration issues preventing the environment from running:
- Updated `requirements.txt` to resolve Django version conflicts.
- Updated `config/settings.py` to use correct `django-csp` 4.0 configuration and `django-axes` backend.

author: backkem
body:
## Summary

Moves `agent-info` message definitions and metadata discovery from the application protocol to the network protocol,
establishing clearer separation of concerns.

## Motivation

Addresses #346: The spec currently links DNS-SD instance names with `agent-info` for consistency checking, creating
tight coupling between discovery and application layers. Since `agent-info` can be exchanged before authentication
completes, protocol implementations need the network layer to control this exchange to maintain security boundaries.

By making `agent-info` a network protocol message, the DNS-SD/agent-info coordination becomes internal to the network
spec rather than a cross-spec dependency.

Also partially relates to #343 by moving `agent-status` (connection keep-alive) to the network protocol as it seems
better suited for transport-specific details.

## Changes

**Network protocol (`network.bs`):**
- Add Metadata Discovery section with `agent-info` message definition
- Add pre-auth message restrictions and abuse protection guidance
- Add Connection Keep-Alive section with `agent-status` messages
- Add Capabilities Registry mechanism

**Application protocol (`application.bs`):**
- Reference network spec for `agent-info` mechanism
- Keep capability value definitions (receive-audio, receive-video, etc.)

**CDDL:**
- Move `agent-info-*`, `agent-status-*`, `request`, `response` to `network_messages.cddl`
- Keep `agent-capability` enum in `application_messages.cddl`

### pnpm has symlink traversal in file:/git dependencies
[CVE-2026-24056](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-24056) / [GHSA-m733-5w8f-5ggw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-m733-5w8f-5ggw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary
When pnpm installs a `file:` (directory) or `git:` dependency, it follows symlinks and reads their target contents without constraining them to the package root. A malicious package containing a symlink to an absolute path (e.g., `/etc/passwd`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa`) causes pnpm to copy that file's contents into `node_modules`, leaking local data.

**Preconditions:** Only affects `file:` and `git:` dependencies. Registry packages (npm) have symlinks stripped during publish and are NOT affected.

##### Details
The vulnerability exists in `store/cafs/src/addFilesFromDir.ts`. The code uses `fs.statSync()` and `readFileSync()` which follow symlinks by default:

```typescript
const absolutePath = path.join(dirname, relativePath)
const stat = fs.statSync(absolutePath)  // Follows symlinks!
const buffer = fs.readFileSync(absolutePath)  // Reads symlink TARGET
```

There is no check that `absolutePath` resolves to a location inside the package directory.

##### PoC
```bash

##### Create malicious package
mkdir -p /tmp/evil && cd /tmp/evil
ln -s /etc/passwd leaked-passwd.txt
echo '{"name":"evil","version":"1.0.0","files":["*.txt"]}' > package.json

##### Victim installs
mkdir /tmp/victim && cd /tmp/victim
pnpm init && pnpm add file:../evil

##### Leaked!
cat node_modules/evil/leaked-passwd.txt
```

##### Impact
- Developers installing local/file dependencies
- CI/CD pipelines installing git dependencies
- Credential theft via symlinks to `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa`

##### Suggested Fix
Use `lstatSync` to detect symlinks and reject those pointing outside the package root in `store/cafs/src/addFilesFromDir.ts`.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.7 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

- [https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/b277b45bc35ae77ca72d7634d144bbd58a48b70f](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/b277b45bc35ae77ca72d7634d144bbd58a48b70f)

</details>

### pnpm has Path Traversal via arbitrary file permission modification 
[CVE-2026-24131](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-24131) / [GHSA-v253-rj99-jwpq](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-v253-rj99-jwpq)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary
When pnpm processes a package's `directories.bin` field, it uses `path.join()` without validating the result stays within the package root. A malicious npm package can specify `"directories": {"bin": "../../../../tmp"}` to escape the package directory, causing pnpm to chmod 755 files at arbitrary locations.

**Note:** Only affects Unix/Linux/macOS. Windows is not affected (`fixBin` gated by `EXECUTABLE_SHEBANG_SUPPORTED`).

##### Details
Vulnerable code in `pkg-manager/package-bins/src/index.ts:15-21`:

```typescript
if (manifest.directories?.bin) {
  const binDir = path.join(pkgPath, manifest.directories.bin)  // NO VALIDATION
  const files = await findFiles(binDir)
  // ... files outside package returned, then chmod 755'd
}
```

The `bin` field IS protected with `isSubdir()` at line 53, but `directories.bin` lacks this check.

##### PoC
```bash

##### Create malicious package
mkdir /tmp/malicious-pkg
echo '{"name":"malicious","version":"1.0.0","directories":{"bin":"../../../../tmp/target"}}' > /tmp/malicious-pkg/package.json

##### Create sensitive file
mkdir -p /tmp/target
echo "secret" > /tmp/target/secret.sh
chmod 600 /tmp/target/secret.sh  # Private

##### Install
pnpm add file:/tmp/malicious-pkg

##### Check permissions
ls -la /tmp/target/secret.sh  # Now 755 (world-readable)
```

##### Impact
- Supply-chain attack via npm packages
- File permissions changed from 600 to 755 (world-readable)
- Affects non-dotfiles in predictable paths (dotfiles excluded by tinyglobby default)

##### Suggested Fix
Add `isSubdir` validation for `directories.bin` paths in `pkg-manager/package-bins/src/index.ts`, matching the existing validation in `commandsFromBin()`:

```typescript
if (manifest.directories?.bin) {
  const binDir = path.join(pkgPath, manifest.directories.bin)
  if (!isSubdir(pkgPath, binDir)) {
    return []  // Reject paths outside package
  }
  // ...
}
```

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.7 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

author: michaelabon
body:
This project has lived through ~10 years of Rails upgrades, and the codebase still contains patterns that made sense in earlier versions but now have better built-in alternatives. rubocop-rails identifies these opportunities to modernize.

Updates to use newer Rails helpers:

- `JSON.parse(response.body)` → `response.parsed_body` Added in Rails 5, handles content-type detection automatically
- `Time.zone.now + 30.minutes` → `30.minutes.from_now` ActiveSupport duration methods have been preferred for years
- String path interpolation → `Rails.root.join/glob` Pathname methods added in Rails 5+ handle cross-platform paths
- `Model.all.pluck` → `Model.pluck` The intermediate `.all` was never necessary
- `where(x).exists?` → `exists?(x)` More direct API that's been available since Rails 4

All new cops are explicitly enabled to maintain consistency with the project's convention of opting into cops rather than relying on defaults.

author: copilot
body:
Java FFM integration received null or invalid `PixelBufferView.data` pointers due to OpenGL PBO unmap/remap cycles and uninitialized state on first frame access.

## Changes

**GLRenderDevice readback lifecycle**
- Persistent PBOs via `glBufferStorage(GL_MAP_PERSISTENT_BIT | GL_MAP_COHERENT_BIT)`
- Map once at initialization, never unmap during operation
- Fence syncs (`glFenceSync`) replace blocking `glFinish()`
- Separate PBO lifecycle from framebuffer resize to preserve pointer stability

**Before:**
```cpp
// end_frame() - race window between unmap and remap
glUnmapBuffer();              // pointer invalidated
color_mapped_ptr_ = nullptr;  // Java can read null here
glGetTexImage(...);
glFinish();                   // blocking
color_mapped_ptr_ = glMapBuffer();
```

**After:**
```cpp
// end_frame() - pointer always valid
glClientWaitSync(color_fence_);  // non-blocking if GPU done
glGetTexImage(...);              // writes to persistently mapped PBO
color_fence_ = glFenceSync();    // track completion
// color_mapped_ptr_ unchanged, always valid
```

**CMakeLists.txt**
- Fixed EGL detection on Linux via pkg-config (FindEGL.cmake doesn't exist)

**Stability guarantees:**
- Pointer non-null after initialization
- Pointer stable across frames and resizes (unless size exceeds capacity)
- Coherent mapping ensures automatic CPU/GPU visibility
- No race conditions

**Requirements:** OpenGL 4.4+ or ARB_buffer_storage extension

> ## Problem Description — Unstable Native Readback Pointer
> 
> ### Summary
> 
> Java intermittently receives a `PixelBufferView` with a null or invalid `data` pointer, causing color buffer acquisition to fail.
> 
> ### Root Cause
> 
> The OpenGL render backend exposes a mapped GPU readback pointer (`PixelBufferView.data`) whose **lifetime is not stable**:
> 
> * The pointer may be **unmapped or not yet mapped** when exposed.
> * Mapping and unmapping occur inside the frame lifecycle.
> * Java assumes the pointer is **always valid and long-lived** once exposed via FFM.
> 
> This creates a timing-dependent race between rendering and buffer consumption.
> 
> ### Consequences
> 
> * First-frame access is undefined.
> * Intermittent failures during normal rendering.
> * Violation of the native ↔ Java ownership contract.
> * Non-deterministic behavior depending on thread timing.

author: t-wy
body:
## Summary

As a deferred Discord application command results in an application webhook that can be used to do the follow-up statelessly, it can be used directly by the bot client to offload a deferred interaction to another stateless machine by providing the webhook url (or equivalently, application id + token) and the interaction data:
```py
# ... handle the received interation data just like what the bot client would do ...

# do the interaction.followup.send statelessly
webhook = discord.Webhook.from_url(
    url = ..., # https://discord(app)?.com/api/webhooks/{application_id}/{token}
    session = await get_session() # an existing aiohttp.ClientSession within the machine process
)
webhook.type = discord.WebhookType.application # it would be nice if Webhook.from_url allows specifying so, but as long as it works
return await webhook.send(content, ephemeral=ephemeral, wait=True, **kwargs) # wait = True is set automatically for application webhook anyways
```

A special case is that this stateless machine may send messages with views.
If persistent views are utilized, it is useful to send a stopped view with interactive components with `custom_id` set, so interactions done by users to the components can still be picked up later by the persistent view in the bot client according to the current Discord.py mechanism.

This PR follows the PR #10089 that allows stateless webhooks to send views. That PR only allows views without dispatchable components to be sent via stateless webhooks.

Unlike normal webhooks, Discord API allows deferred application interactions follow-up `send` to act like a direct `send_message` call in most scenarios since it's introduced without restrictions in normal stateless webhooks as addressed in #10089.

The `is_finished` condition followed exactly as the condition that checks whether to do `self._state.store_view` later, i.e.
```py
if view is not MISSING and not view.is_finished() and view.is_dispatchable():
    message_id = None if msg is None else msg.id
    self._state.store_view(view, message_id)
```
, which infers that a "finished" view is already inherently supported by this coroutine method.

Therefore, the current _WebhookState ValueError check done in discord.py does not need to block finished views from being sent, as a "finished" view used this way would not be `store`d or `wait`ed to trigger callbacks anyways. This unlocks the full potential for application webhooks initialized without any client state to work.

## Checklist

author: copilot
body:
Original prompt > > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > [MergeDuplicates] Unreliable SignalR > Prompt: > > I use SignalR for the C# backend to tell the frontend React app that the user-requested data is ready. Some users in a location with some connectivity issues are reporting that the frontend is indefinitely waiting for the response, which the backend should have finished within a few seconds. However, the tunnel is neither closed nor disconnected. How might that happen? > > Claude Sonnet 4.5 response: > > This sounds like a SignalR message delivery failure where the connection remains alive but the actual message gets lost. Here are the most likely causes: > > ## Message Loss Scenarios > > **Network packet loss without TCP disconnection** - The most probable cause. TCP can keep the connection alive via keepalives while still dropping application-layer messages. SignalR messages can get lost if packets are dropped but not retransmitted properly, especially on poor mobile/WiFi networks. > > **Server-to-client buffer overflow** - If the server sends messages faster than the client can receive them over a slow connection, the SignalR transport buffer may drop messages. This is more common with Server-Sent Events (SSE) transport than WebSockets. > > **Transport fallback issues** - If using LongPolling as a fallback, there's a window where messages can be lost during transport negotiation or when switching transports mid-session. > > **Load balancer/proxy interference** - Intermediary infrastructure might buffer or drop messages while keeping the connection alive, particularly with reverse proxies that have aggressive timeouts on streaming responses. > > ## Practical Solutions > > 1. **Implement message acknowledgment**: > ```csharp > // Server > await Clients.Caller.SendAsync("DataReady", requestId, data); > // Wait for ack or implement retry logic > ``` > > ```javascript > // Client - explicitly acknowledge > connection.on("DataReady", (requestId, data) => { > connection.invoke("AcknowledgeData", requestId); > // process data > }); > ``` > > 2. **Add application-level timeouts on the frontend** - Don't rely solely on SignalR connection state. Set a timeout (e.g., 30 seconds) and poll via HTTP if SignalR doesn't deliver. > > 3. **Configure connection resilience**: > ```csharp > // Server > services.AddSignalR(options => { > options.KeepAliveInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10); > options.ClientTimeoutInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30); > }); > ``` > > 4. **Force WebSockets only** for critical messages if possible - it has better reliability than other transports: > ```javascript > const connection = new signalR.HubConnectionBuilder() > .withUrl("/hub", { > transport: signalR.HttpTransportType.WebSockets > }) > .build(); > ``` > > 5. **Add fallback polling** - If no SignalR response within X seconds, have the client make a REST API call to check if the data is actually ready. > > The acknowledgment pattern combined with a client-side timeout is your most robust solution for spotty connections. > > Plan solution 1: "Implement message acknowledgment". Wait for approval to proceed with plan. > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > >

body:
### Motivation
- Make the CDP PDF printout visually match the existing "Solicitud de Compra" PDF and include missing metadata (justificación, logos, signatures, correlativo) while not changing CDP/CDO persistence or business logic.
- Restrict printing to the same admin/budget roles and provide a minimal, xhtml2pdf-friendly template that renders reliably (avoid changing models or permission rules).

### Description
- Added a reusable permission helper `puede_imprimir_cdp(user)` in `upcv_app/scompras_app/utils.py` to allow printing only to `Administrador` or `PRESUPUESTO` users.
- Implemented `generar_pdf_cdp` view in `upcv_app/scompras_app/views.py` that enforces `puede_imprimir_cdp`, builds a print-only context including `cdp_correlativo_5 = str(cdp.id).zfill(5)`, `justificacion`, `solicitante_nombre`, `solicitante_cargo`, `encargado_nombre`, and absolute `logo` URLs, and streams the PDF via xhtml2pdf.
- Reworked `upcv_app/scompras_app/templates/scompras/cdp_pdf.html` to mirror `solicitud_pdf.html` header/logo/frames, show the 5-digit CDP correlativo, include the solicitud justification, render the renglones table with `money_gtq` formatting, and add the two-column signatures and footer frames for xhtml2pdf compatibility.
- Exposed `puede_imprimir_cdp` to the solicitud detail view context and added an "🖨️ Imprimir CDP" button in `templates/scompras/detalle_solicitud.html` that opens the new PDF route; registered the URL `path('cdp/<int:cdp_id>/pdf/', views.generar_pdf_cdp, name='generar_pdf_cdp')` in `urls.py`.
- Did not modify models, existing CDP/CDO/solicitud logic, groups, or permissions beyond the new print helper.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change (no CI/test run was requested or performed).

author: akobirbaratov
body:
⚡ Bolt: Memoize ChatMessage to optimize streaming performance

💡 **What:** 
Implemented \`React.memo\` for the \`ChatMessage\` component and \`useMemo\` for the chat history transformation in the \`Home\` component.

🎯 **Why:** 
In the previous implementation, every new chunk of text received during assistant streaming triggered a re-render of the entire chat history. For a conversation with N messages, this resulted in O(N) re-renders per chunk, causing significant performance degradation as the history grew.

📊 **Impact:** 
- Reduces re-renders from O(N*M) to O(M) during streaming, where N is conversation length and M is chunk count.
- In a test with 4 messages, total re-renders during a short stream dropped from 78 to 30 (~60% reduction). 
- For long conversations (e.g., 20+ messages), the improvement will be >90%.

🔬 **Measurement:** 
Verified using temporary \`console.count\` instrumentation in a Playwright test environment. Observed that older messages no longer re-render when the latest message is being updated. Passed \`bun run lint\` and \`bun run build\`.

- Decorated the ESI contract dropdown label to include an `issuerLabel` that is either the character name, `Issuer #<id>`, or `Issuer unknown` as a fallback.
- Added an `Issuer:` line to the contract details card that formats the same `issuerLabel` for the selected contract.
- Kept existing behavior for resolving start/end names and preserved reward/volume/collateral comparison logic.

## Description

Wire up the `--debug` flag to show full exception tracebacks when errors occur. This makes debugging much easier.

## Related Issue

Closes #43

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- Wire up `--debug` flag to configure logging level (DEBUG when enabled, WARNING otherwise)
- Add `is_debug_mode()` utility to check debug state from Click context
- Add `print_exception()` utility that shows full traceback in debug mode
- Update 10 CLI commands to use `print_exception()` for error handling

## Usage

```bash
# Without debug - shows only error message
nf cache refresh cluster1
# cluster1: Failed - 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte...

# With debug - shows full traceback
nf --debug cache refresh cluster1
# cluster1: Failed - 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte...
# Traceback (most recent call last):
#   File "...", line X, in ...
#   ...
```

## Testing

- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] Manually verified traceback appears with --debug

author: copilot
body:
Implements a complete self-hosted Git platform in JavaScript with distributed cluster execution, real-time collaboration, and integrated VSCode web editor.

## Core Platform

**Authentication & Authorization**
- JWT-based auth with configurable password hashing (bcrypt/argon2)
- Three-tier role system: Admin, Moderator, User
- First registered user auto-promoted to admin
- User and IP ban management with history tracking

**Repository Management**
- Native git initialization with bare repos at `Z:/mnt/repos/{owner}/{repo}`
- Compression level 9 for minimal storage footprint
- Full Git HTTP protocol (clone, push, pull)
- Auto-generated README on repo creation
- Git internals (.git, HEAD, refs) filtered from file browser

**Organizations & Social**
- Organization creation and team management
- User/org profiles with follow system
- Collaborator permissions (read/write)
- Contributor tracking from git log

## CI/CD & Clusters

**Pipeline System**
- YAML-based configuration (`.codara-ci.yml`)
- Matrix builds with parallel execution
- Smart caching with fallback keys
- Artifact collection and archiving
- Live log streaming via WebSocket
- Secrets vault with encryption

**Distributed Execution**
- Cluster agent software in `cluster/` directory
- Auto-discovery via UDP broadcast + full IP range scanning
- Power-based classification: high (16GB+) vs low (<16GB)
- Permission-based cluster access control
- Shared storage on Z: drive for all jobs and repos
- Load balancing with failover support

```javascript
// Cluster discovers jobs from shared directory
Z:/mnt/runners/jobs/{job_id}/
  ├── job.json          // Config from main site
  ├── workspace/        // Execution environment
  ├── artifacts/        // Build outputs
  └── logs/output.log   // Streamed to client
```

## React UI

**Pages & Features**
- Login/signup with comprehensive registration (DOB, country)
- Dashboard with theme toggle (dark/light)
- Repository view with tabs: Code, Issues, PRs, Commits
- File browser with syntax highlighting and line numbers
- Admin panel: user management, platform stats, ban controls
- Search with filters (repos, orgs, users)
- Explore page for trending projects
- User/org profiles with followers/following

**VSCode Integration**
- Isolated VSCode instance per repository
- Real-time collaboration with cursor tracking
- Live file updates via operational transformation
- Project chat for contributors
- Terminal disabled for security

## Issues & PRs

- Issue creation with labels and comments
- Pull request workflow with merge/close
- State management (open/closed/merged)
- Comment threads on both

## Technical Stack

**Backend:** Node.js, Express, SQLite/PostgreSQL, simple-git  
**Frontend:** React, Vite, React Router  
**Real-time:** WebSocket for collaboration and logs  
**Queue:** Bull with Redis (optional, in-memory fallback)  

**Storage Structure:**
```
Z:/mnt/
├── repos/{owner}/{repo}/     # Git bare repos
├── runners/jobs/{job_id}/    # CI/CD execution
├── cache/{project_id}/       # Build cache
└── app.ini                   # Platform config
```

## API Surface

60+ endpoints covering:
- Auth: `/api/auth/*`
- Repos: `/api/repositories/*`, `/api/:owner/:repo/*`
- Git: `/api/:owner/:repo/commits`, `/api/:owner/:repo/branches`
- Issues: `/api/:owner/:repo/issues/*`
- PRs: `/api/:owner/:repo/pulls/*`
- Admin: `/api/admin/*`, `/api/bans/*`
- Clusters: `/api/clusters/*`
- CI/CD: `/api/cicd/*`
- Search: `/api/search`, `/api/explore`
- Social: `/api/profile/:user`, `/api/notifications`

## Screenshots

**Dashboard - Dark Theme**
![Dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f331e982-0fa5-4b4f-8f9c-25874d104df8)

**Dashboard - Light Theme**
![Light Mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d2b269c-13b0-4ebd-8128-c719db8d1666)

**Repository Page**
![Repository](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/333cc619-e68b-4f31-a4a9-fbd230e73515)

**VSCode Web Editor**
![VSCode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa9ee665-89dc-4deb-9692-95bc08ad09ae)

**Admin Panel**
![Admin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10b65526-4169-41d0-94b4-98841057d894)

## Configuration

All paths configurable via environment variables. Production uses Z: drive for shared cluster access; development uses local paths. Config file at `Z:/mnt/app.ini` for platform settings (admin privileges, security, features).

## Build & Deploy

```bash
npm install && cd client && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
npm start  # Serves React app from dist/, API on port 3000
```

Cluster agent deployed separately to worker nodes with system service installation script.

body:
### Description

Adds `applicantReadAcls` to `StoredFileAcls` as a record of which Applicants can access the file.

This is supplementary to the existing mechanism of storing the authorized Applicant ID in the file name path and as such should have no effect for now. It will be materially utilized in the upcoming improved merge logic, where we will move data from one Applicant to another and delete the former. In that case this the Acl for the delete applicant's files will be updated with the maintained applicants ID, ensuring the User can still access them.

There is no specific interaction with either cloud provider, in particular Azure which stores file names with a GUID, as it only changes the file name part of the key and not the path.

`applicantReadAcls` will not be present in previous `StoredFileAcls` json blobs and the code and tests address that.

[Design Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qq5lLXMgAxMvrsZzcyKEmZsQAtnCt6lcpkqQ836IWhE/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.dtae2iqc49dq)



## Release notes

Adds explicit applicant ID access controls for files. The utility of this will come when the account merging improvements are finished.

## Summary
- Fixes #445: Fetching full content doesn't work for some feeds
- The "Fetch Full Content" button was silently failing for entries that had a previous fetch attempt that errored
- Now clicking the button properly triggers a retry when there was a previous error

## Changes
- **EntryContent.tsx**: Updated `handleToggleFetchFullContent` to check for `fullContentError` in addition to `fullContentFetchedAt`
- **EntryContent.tsx**: Updated auto-fetch `useEffect` to retry when there was a previous error
- **EntryContentBody.tsx**: Added "Retry Fetch" button state with error styling (red border/text) when there's a `fullContentError`
- Added tooltip showing the error message on hover

## Root Cause
The code was checking `!entry.fullContentFetchedAt` to decide whether to trigger a fetch, but `fullContentFetchedAt` is set even when the fetch fails. So entries with previous failed fetches would never retry.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open an entry from a feed where full content fetch previously failed
- [ ] Verify the button shows "Retry Fetch" with red styling
- [ ] Hover over button to see error tooltip
- [ ] Click the button and verify fetch is triggered
